articles.title: Aaron Rodgers blasts Mike McCarthy on Pat McAfee show after Steelers bench him, calls for major coaching changes
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers had plenty to get off his chest, and his latest appearance on The Pat McAfee Show quickly turned into a major talking point for Pittsburgh
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers had plenty to get off his chest, and his latest appearance on The Pat McAfee Show quickly turned into a major talking point for Pittsburgh Steelers fans. After being benched ahead of the team's Week 12 matchup against the Denver Broncos, the veteran quarterback finally addressed the situation, and his comments about head coach Mike McCarthy added another layer of drama to an already difficult week in Pittsburgh.Rodgers was expected to lead the Steelers against Denver, but the team made a surprising decision to make him inactive and hand the starting job to Mason Rudolph. The move raised questions about Rodgers' future, especially with the season entering a crucial stretch.Aaron Rodgers reveals how he found out about Steelers' benchingOne of the biggest revelations from Rodgers' appearance was how he learned about the decision. According to his account, he found out he would not be playing after receiving a phone call from Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth the previous night.The timing made the situation even more surprising, considering Rodgers had spoken publicly earlier in the week as though he expected to play. His sudden change in status left fans wondering what had happened behind closed doors.Rodgers makes uncomfortable claims about Mike McCarthyHowever, the conversation took an even more interesting turn when Rodgers began discussing McCarthy.The quarterback reportedly claimed that McCarthy had fallen asleep during team meetings. He also alleged that the head coach had mistakenly referred to the Steelers as the Green Bay Packers, his former team.Rodgers' reaction to the alleged mix-up was particularly telling. He reportedly questioned what was happening and where McCarthy's head was at.The comments were especially notable given their history together in Green Bay. Rodgers and McCarthy spent years working together with the Packers, winning a Super Bowl during their time together. Their relationship was not always smooth, making these latest remarks even more intriguing.Aaron Rodgers wants bigger changes in Pittsburgh?Rodgers also reportedly suggested that the Steelers would benefit from changing their play-caller and potentially even their head coach. That is a significant statement from a veteran quarterback, particularly at a time when Pittsburgh is dealing with questions about its offensive direction and leadership.With Rudolph now taking over under center, the Steelers have another major decision to navigate. Meanwhile, Rodgers' comments have shifted attention away from the quarterback change and toward the coaching staff.Whether this is the beginning of a bigger fallout between Rodgers and McCarthy remains to be seen. But one thing is certain: Rodgers' appearance on McAfee's show has given Steelers fans plenty to discuss, and the questions surrounding his future in Pittsburgh are unlikely to disappear anytime soon.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. While Jason Kelce has been able to balance his professional and professional commitments ever since he became a father, he has been public about what he has struggled with.Jason Kelce reflected on how he has struggled with a few issues that have distracted himA few months ago, Jason Kelce answered a fan’s question on his podcast about his favorite apps on his phone as he said, "I would have no apps, and I would throw my phone into a volcano of magma because I hate how much I'm on my phone.”The former Philadelphia Eagles’ icon added, “I hate everything to do with my phone. articles.title: Mike McCarthy says it was his call to bench Aaron Rodgers, denies several claims made by former Steelers QB
articles.summary: Rodgers' rant went heavy on criticizing Mike McCarthy after he was benched.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy spoke to the media Wednesday afternoon. While the topic would have focused on the team's game Friday against the Denver Broncos, the news conference was overshadowed by the scorched-earth rant quarterback Aaron Rodgers gave earlier in the day on "The Pat McAfee Show," which prompted the team to release him shortly afterward .

McCarthy took the podium and began by telling the media he was focused on Friday's matchup against Denver. The head coach was, of course, asked about some of Rodgers' accusations.

McCarthy said it was his decision to bench Rodgers for Friday's game and give the start to backup Mason Rudolph. On why the announcement came after 11 p.m. ET on Tuesday night, McCarthy said they had to contact Rodgers' agent, but that they had made "consistent efforts to do so" Tuesday evening.

"There was an ultimatum made, clearly outside of his job description, so it was my decision to bench him," McCarthy said. The head coach declined to elaborate on the demand.

According to multiple reports Wednesday night, that ultimatum was Rodgers demanding full control of play-calling or else he wanted to be released. Steelers insider Gerry Dulac reported : "In a Tuesday evening meeting, Aaron Rodgers gave Mike Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: I want to call all the plays or just release me. They called his bluff and released him."

Before his formal release, the veteran QB had claimed earlier Wednesday that he learned about his benching only after tight end Pat Freiermuth told him.

Rodgers also claimed that McCarthy still blames the quarterback for getting the head coach fired from the Green Bay Packers. McCarthy did not expand on this claim and simply said, "That's not accurate."

McCarthy was asked about Rodgers' claims that the head coach had lost the locker room. He responded by saying that he came from a player meeting and that it was "direct and very honest." McCarthy said he is "proud of our leadership. More importantly, I love the urgency coming out of that meeting."

The head coach was asked how he knows he is still the right person for this job. He said, "I know how to win. And that's the facts. This is my third program, and I plan on winning here." McCarthy acknowledged that this situation is a growth opportunity he intends to take advantage of.

One of the biggest claims Rodgers made was that during halftime of last week's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, McCarthy had broken down a team huddle, saying "1-2-3, Packers!" He addressed those claims and said, "Halftime was very emotional; there were conversations prior to that embarrassing moment. We work a lot of hours, definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments."

McCarthy said he met with players leadership Wednesday and admitted it was a focus he should have addressed earlier in his tenure, when he took over from former head coach Mike Tomlin.

One of Rodgers' focal-point claims about McCarthy was that the head coach consistently fell asleep in team meetings. This claim was not addressed during the news conference.

The Steelers are reportedly not expected to make any drastic move with McCarthy, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . The head coach said Wednesday that the organization has fully supported him through everything said publicly.

The Steelers officially released Rodgers on Wednesday afternoon. If he clears waivers, he will become a free agent.

articles.title: Tony Romo's first gig since CBS exit involves 'predictions' at Jake Paul-led company
articles.summary: The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster is joining Jake Paul-founded gaming company Betr as its "Chief Predictions Officer."
articles.body:
Tony Romo is back in the game – sort of.

The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster is joining gaming company Betr as its "Chief Predictions Officer." Betr was cofounded by Jake Paul.

After retiring following the 2016 season, Romo had been the NFL on CBS' lead game analyst. However, he and the network parted ways in October following his July arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated .

"Tony Romo has built an extraordinary reputation around something that sits at the very heart of our business: predictions," Betr CEO and cofounder Joey Levy said in a statement. "His ability to see what's coming before anyone else has made him one of the most compelling personalities in sports, and we see a tremendous opportunity to bring that talent and personality to our growing ecosystem."

Former Cowboys QB Tony Romo's career in photos

According to The Hollywood Reporter , Romo's role will consist of him "appearing in original content, delivering sport-related prediction and serving as a face of the brand in marketing." He'll appear in videos for social media alongside Paul.

"I've spent my entire career trying to anticipate what's going to happen next, whether that was on the field or in the broadcast booth," Romo said in a statement. "Now I get to put those instincts to work in a completely new way with Betr. What Jake, Joey and the team are building is really interesting because they're bringing so many different ways for fans to engage with sports and gaming together in one place. I'm looking forward to having some fun, making predictions and being part of where this company is headed. And I've got a pretty good feeling about what's coming next."

Romo has been replaced in CBS' top NFL booth by JJ Watt , who now sits alongside Jim Nantz. Romo's first appearance in the public spotlight following his arrest, which included embarrassing body camera footage from the police, came during a "Monday Night Football" alternate broadcast stream with Pat McAfee.

articles.title: “He’s the real deal": Travis Kelce revealed why he believed Patrick Mahomes could become the NFL's best
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes had yet to establish himself as an NFL superstar when Travis Kelce began talking about his extraordinary potential.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had yet to establish himself as an NFL superstar when Travis Kelce began talking about his extraordinary potential. In early 2018, the Kansas City Chiefs were preparing for a major change at quarterback after trading Alex Smith to Washington. Mahomes was stepping into a demanding role, but Kelce already believed the young passer could take the team to another level. His comments from that period became particularly interesting when Mahomes eventually delivered one of the greatest debut seasons by a starting quarterback in NFL history.Travis Kelce made a bold Patrick Mahomes prediction in March 2018Travis Kelce shared his confidence during an interview with SiriusXM NFL Radio on March 23, 2018. He discussed the difference between Patrick Mahomes and Alex Smith, particularly their approach to throwing the football.“I think, one, he brings confidence,” Kelce said of Mahomes. “He’s going to sling that thing around a little bit more, a little bit different than Alex did. Alex is the guy where, if he sees you’re open, he’ll chuck it. But he might not always throw you open. It has to be a certain situation that he feels comfortable in that regard. And I think Pat is a guy, if you’re out there and his eyes are on you, he’s going to either throw you open or he’s going to put it on the money when you are open.”Kelce then made a prediction that stood out even more as Mahomes' career progressed.“When [Mahomes] gets out of pocket, he’s a little bit more downfield aware, where Alex, he’s got them scooter legs on him; I always call him ‘Scooter.’ He can scoot now, so he has the ability to hurt you with the legs. It’s definitely a different style of quarterbacking, but at the same time, just as Alex was one of the best in the league this year, I think Pat can be the best in the league this year.”The tight end had also backed Mahomes following Smith's departure in January 2018. Speaking about the quarterback's abilities, Kelce said, “I feel like Patty Cakes can come in and roll the dice on anybody.”He added, “He can throw the ball any way, he can throw it off his back foot and he can jump and throw, he can throw the ball anywhere, any way you need for it to be thrown. His confidence is definitely one of the best attributes to his game.”Patrick Mahomes eventually proved Travis Kelce rightInterestingly, Kelce later admitted that Mahomes' performances still surprised him. During an appearance on the Dan Patrick Show on September 25, 2018, he recalled when he became fully convinced.“I personally—I wasn’t fully on board until that first game (in 2018).”He also praised Mahomes after watching his early performances, saying, “He’s the real deal.”Mahomes finished the 2018 regular season with 5,097 passing yards, 50 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. He won the NFL MVP award in February 2019, becoming the youngest quarterback to receive the honour at that time.Kelce was equally productive, recording 103 receptions, 1,336 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns.What began as a bold prediction in March 2018 eventually became reality. Mahomes became an MVP, while Kelce emerged as one of his most trusted targets. Their partnership helped shape the Chiefs' success for years.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' playing future in doubt as five NFL teams emerge as potential destinations following Steelers release
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers' final NFL season has taken an unexpected turn.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers' final NFL season has taken an unexpected turn. What began as a reunion with former Green Bay Packers coach Mike McCarthy has ended in a public fallout, a benching and now his release from the Pittsburgh Steelers. At 42, Rodgers suddenly finds himself facing a career-defining decision. He can walk away from football or look for one last opportunity elsewhere. Several teams could use an experienced quarterback, but the bigger question is whether Rodgers still has enough left to make a difference.Aaron Rodgers' Steelers release puts Ravens and Patriots in the picturePittsburgh's decision to move on from Rodgers followed a growing disagreement with McCarthy. The quarterback reportedly criticised the coach's approach during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, describing it as "disrespectful to the game itself."Rodgers also revealed concerns about McCarthy's preparation and involvement during training camp. He said, "I'm talking about in training camp when this stuff was going on, when he was missing meetings and the word was he's sleeping and then he's sleeping in the coaches' film sessions and he's not alert here." Rodgers told The Pat McAfee Show. "And he doesn't want to get to know the defense."The fallout proved costly. Pittsburgh had initially planned to keep Rodgers after benching him in favour of Mason Rudolph. However, the situation changed, and the veteran quarterback will now enter waivers. If no team claims him, he can negotiate with any franchise.The Baltimore Ravens could consider Rodgers if Lamar Jackson remains unavailable because of his thumb injury. Jacoby Brissett is already in Baltimore, but two consecutive losses could encourage the organisation to explore another option.The New England Patriots also deserve attention. Drake Maye's fractured fibula has created uncertainty at quarterback, leaving Tommy DeVito as the leading available option. Rodgers' experience could give New England a more reliable presence during its playoff push.Eagles, Falcons and Packers emerge as Aaron Rodgers landing spotsThe Philadelphia Eagles represent another possibility, although their 3-7 record makes the move difficult to justify. Injuries and inconsistent quarterback play have hurt their season. Rodgers could bring stability while working alongside offensive talents such as Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert.Atlanta could offer an even more interesting opportunity. The Falcons have Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, but Michael Penix Jr.'s struggles have raised questions. Rodgers' experience could help an offence with considerable potential.There are also emergency options. The Minnesota Vikings could revisit their interest if Kirk Cousins gets injured. A return to the Green Bay Packers is another possibility if Jordan Love becomes unavailable. Jacksonville could also enter the conversation if Trevor Lawrence suffers an injury.Rodgers previously indicated that 2026 would be his final NFL season. Whether he chooses to honour that decision or pursue one last playoff opportunity remains uncertain. His next move could determine how his remarkable career comes to an end.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Only 1 NFL team makes sense for Aaron Rodgers, and even it comes with a caveat
articles.summary: There are not many clear options if Aaron Rodgers wants to keep playing. Even the most likely landing spot might not be a perfect fit.
articles.body:
There aren't too many teams that make sense right now for Aaron Rodgers.

Another reason: There aren't too many obvious football fits right now.

If all you do is comb through the list of potentially QB-needy teams right now, in terms of strictly needing help down the stretch, it's not that long. Especially when that quarterback is 43 years old next week, largely struggling on the field and willing to publicly question his head coach.

Perhaps Rodgers is done, and this is his way of announcing it. But maybe he's not done and harbors hope that he can finish out what's presumably his final NFL season on something of a high note.

Is there a team that would give him that opportunity? Here are some of the potential options, ranked in descending order — and those odds get pretty low the farther down the list we go:

Strictly from a football standpoint, there's some sense, especially if you're not the biggest Tommy DeVito enthusiast. With Drake Maye injured, and possibly for the duration of the season, the Patriots are nominally still in the race at 5-5. With at least four tough games remaining, the margin for error is slim.

Rodgers could be viewed as an upgrade over DeVito, and there'd be no reasonable undercutting of Maye, who is out indefinitely. This would be the kind of arrangement that lasts a month or two, no longer.

Rodgers considers Mike Vrabel a friend. It's fair to wonder if that friendship still exists after Rodgers has several times brought up how the Vrabel-Dianna Russini story has been covered in the media, calling it improper handling and pointing out the potential conflicts of interest involved in the story.

That might be enough for the Patriots to cross their fingers and hope for miracle work from Tommy Cutlets. Or perhaps Vrabel and Rodgers could see past that for the next several weeks. Hard to say.

For fans of revenge narratives, the Ravens belong on your list. Tableau: Rodgers signs with Baltimore, Jacoby Brissett gets hurt and it's Rodgers vs. Mason Rudolph in Baltimore, Week 18, with a playoff spot on the line. Can't script 'em much better than that.

Realistically? The Ravens probably won't sign Rodgers. It certainly would be fun to consider, and there could be a possibility if Brissett can't go and Lamar Jackson is unable to return from a thumb injury, but a few things likely would need to happen before this is even considered.

Heck, if Philip Rivers can come out of retirement and play for the Colts four years removed from the NFL, what makes Rodgers landing in Indianapolis so wild? Again, this would strictly be from a football standpoint, and it would take the Colts being completely done with Anthony Richardson Sr. to feel probable. Even Rodgers might pass on playing with the Colts considering where they're at. And they've already faced the Steelers, so the revenge possibility is a non-factor.

Similar situation to the Colts in that it could be a football need, but there's also the connection to Cards offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett, one of Rodgers' favorite assistant coaches over the years. If Carson Beck's back injury continues to flare up, perhaps Rodgers rates as an upgrade over Josh Johnson. Rodgers has no meaningful relationship with Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur, but as everyone knows, Rodgers did play for LaFleur's brother, Matt, for many years in Green Bay.

This would be a contingency situation only, as Brock Purdy is playing at an MVP level and the Niners have one of the better backups in the league in Mac Jones. The connection here is thin, but Rodgers has called Kyle Shanahan a "phenomenal play-caller" and "fantastic coach," and Shanahan did reach out to Matt LaFleur to inquire about trading for Rodgers. This one feels thin at best, but not impossible.

articles.title: Drew Allar’s reaction to Aaron Rodgers’ Pittsburgh Steelers fallout gets cut short in awkward locker room moment
articles.summary: Drew Allar found himself caught in an uncomfortable moment in the Pittsburgh Steelers' locker room after offering a brief reaction to Aaron Rodgers'
articles.body: Drew Allar found himself caught in an uncomfortable moment in the Pittsburgh Steelers' locker room after offering a brief reaction to Aaron Rodgers' departure. The rookie quarterback had barely finished sharing his thoughts when veteran safety DeShon Elliott stepped in and stopped the media exchange. The interruption came amid a heated fallout between Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy, leaving Allar reluctant to get drawn into a dispute that had quickly taken over the Steelers' headlines.Allar had spent time learning from Rodgers since joining Pittsburgh, making his response more personal than a routine comment on a quarterback change. However, Elliott's intervention cut the conversation short, adding another unexpected moment to an already turbulent situation in Pittsburgh.DeShon Elliott stops Drew Allar from speaking further on Aaron RodgersAllar did not criticize Rodgers or McCarthy. Instead, he expressed his disappointment at seeing the veteran's time in Pittsburgh take such a turn and acknowledged the lessons he had picked up from the four-time MVP.“For me, it’s kind of sad to see. Because I have a lot of respect for Aaron. I’ve learned a lot from him since he’s been here. I’m just going to leave it at that and wish Aaron the best.”Allar shared those thoughts during the Steelers' locker-room media availability after practice. However, Elliott soon walked over, made a gesture indicating that the rookie should stop speaking and called out, “Drew!”According to Pittsburgh Tribune-Review reporter Chris Adamski, the media scrum ended immediately after the interruption. Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reporter Ray Fittipaldo also reported that Elliott approached Allar and told him to stop the interview.The moment unfolded while Rodgers was airing his grievances against McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show. Allar acknowledged that he knew about Rodgers' comments but indicated that he had only just finished practice. He also made it clear that he did not consider himself the right person to confirm or deny the allegations against the head coach.That reluctance is understandable. The rookie has spent much of his early time in Pittsburgh learning rather than playing, and getting caught in a public dispute between the quarterback and head coach would hardly help his development.Aaron Rodgers’ fallout with Mike McCarthy leaves Pittsburgh Steelers in turmoilThe Steelers benched Rodgers and named Mason Rudolph their starter for the upcoming game against the Denver Broncos. The decision came after McCarthy had publicly backed Rodgers earlier in the week, making the change particularly surprising.Rodgers, meanwhile, made several allegations about McCarthy's conduct during his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show. He claimed the coach arrived late to a quarterback meeting, fell asleep during it and missed other team activities.The quarterback also recalled Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, claiming McCarthy mistakenly ended a halftime huddle by saying, “1-2-3 Packers!” Rodgers presented the incident as another example of the disconnect he believed had developed between the coach and players. These allegations remain Rodgers' account of events.He also said he had raised concerns about the offensive operation and play-calling before the benching. Rodgers claimed he told McCarthy to release him if the coach intended to bench him. When asked about a possible return, he made his position clear.“That ship has sailed.”Following the interview, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Pittsburgh planned to release Rodgers, citing Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. NFL Network subsequently reported that the Steelers were waiving the veteran quarterback.The Steelers now turn to Rudolph, with Will Howard and Allar also in the quarterback room. Pittsburgh selected Allar 76th overall in the third round of the NFL Draft, but the Penn State product had remained inactive through the team's first 10 games.Allar was expected to serve as the emergency third quarterback against Denver. Under the NFL's emergency quarterback rule, he can enter the game only if both quarterbacks ahead of him cannot continue because of injuries.As of now, Allar remains a rookie trying to learn his way through the NFL. Yet his interrupted interview offered a glimpse of how quickly the Rodgers-McCarthy dispute has spilled beyond the two men at its centre.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: What is Tony Romo’s new job with Jake Paul? Former Dallas Cowboys QB finds fresh role after CBS exit
articles.summary: Tony Romo has found a new professional home after his departure from CBS, and his latest move takes him into the sports gaming business.
articles.body: Tony Romo has found a new professional home after his departure from CBS, and his latest move takes him into the sports gaming business. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback has joined Jake Paul’s Betr as its Chief Predictions Officer. The role puts Romo back in the spotlight, although this time, he will work on sports predictions and content rather than NFL commentary from the broadcast booth.What does Tony Romo's Chief Predictions Officer role at Betr involve?Romo announced his new position on X recently, writing, “I’m Back. New Job. Same Goal. Extremely excited to announce I have joined @betr as their Chief Predictions Officer 🔮.”Betr is a sports gaming and entertainment company founded by Jake Paul and Joey Levy. Its platform offers gaming products built around sports predictions, alongside other gaming features. The company also develops sports-related content to attract fans who follow athletes, teams and major sporting events.As Chief Predictions Officer, Romo will become a prominent face of the Betr brand. The company plans to use his football knowledge and ability to read the game across its gaming products and content. He will also hold an equity stake in Betr, giving him an ownership interest rather than simply serving as a promotional figure.Romo explained his excitement about the opportunity, saying he could use the instincts he developed during his playing and broadcasting career in a different setting.“I’ve spent my entire career trying to anticipate what’s going to happen next, whether that was on the field or in the broadcast booth. Now I get to put those instincts to work in a completely new way with Betr…” he said in the announcement.He also expressed enthusiasm about making predictions, enjoying the experience and contributing to the company's future.Jake Paul welcomed Romo in a video accompanying the announcement. The boxer and influencer, who co-founded Betr, expressed excitement about bringing the former NFL quarterback into the company as it looks to expand its presence in sports gaming and entertainment. Tony Romo moves on after CBS Sports departureRomo's new position follows a difficult stretch in his broadcasting career. He and CBS Sports mutually parted ways in October, ending his run as one of the network's leading NFL analysts alongside Jim Nantz. The network subsequently continued with its plans for the lead broadcast team, with J.J. Watt stepping into the role.The separation came after Romo's July arrest for operating while intoxicated in Wisconsin. He pleaded no contest to the charge in September, resulting in a six-month suspension of his driving privileges and an alcohol assessment program.Romo had previously addressed the situation in a statement, saying he intended to step away and focus on his personal life before pursuing another opportunity.“I’m going to use this time to take a break, something I’ve never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity,” he wrote.He did not remain away from football for long. Romo appeared on the Pat McAfee alternate broadcast of the Bills-Vikings Monday Night Football game earlier this month. McAfee welcomed him back to live commentary, calling him a quarterback expert and expressing appreciation for his return.Now, Betr gives Romo a different platform to use his football knowledge. His experience as a former NFL quarterback and longtime broadcaster offers the company a recognizable voice, while the new role allows Romo to explore a career outside traditional television commentary.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Buffalo’s 9-1 record has given the Bills plenty of reasons to feel confident, but Josh Allen’s recent performances have raised questions about his decision-making. ESPN analyst Mina Kimes believes the quarterback is repeating mistakes that have troubled him in the past. Ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs’ Thanksgiving night visit, she pointed to forced throws, missed receivers and poor choices when plays break down. Allen threw two interceptions against Miami, yet Buffalo won 26-9. The result was comfortable. His performance was not. With Kansas City waiting, Allen has little time to correct the issues.Mina Kimes sees old problems returning in Josh Allen’s gameSpeaking on “The Mina Kimes Show featuring Lenny,” Kimes said Josh Allen’s recent play reminded her of earlier periods in his career. Her concern was not simply about the interceptions. She believes Allen sometimes decides that nobody is open before fully working through his options.There are times when the coverage leaves Allen with little room to operate. Kimes acknowledged that. But she also sees him forcing throws into tight windows and missing chances when receivers do get separation.“I think if I had to diagnose, like, what I’m seeing, that’s probably the main culprit,” Kimes added.The issue becomes more serious when Buffalo’s offense cannot rely on its running game. Allen may feel he has to create something with his arm, especially when the receivers struggle to get open. Yet that pressure can lead to risky decisions.“They haven’t been dominant on the ground. It just feels like there are plays where no one’s open… And then even when someone is open, there are moments when it feels like he’s not seeing it well,” Kimes said.That distinction is important. Allen is not being asked to avoid every difficult throw. He needs to recognize when a play has a simpler answer. A missed completion can leave Buffalo behind the chains. A forced pass can hand the opponent the ball.Kimes also praised Miami’s defense, which made life difficult for Allen throughout the game. She singled out the pass rush and gave credit to Chop Robinson.“I was genuinely impressed by the Dolphins’ defense in this game. Chop Robinson, by the way, has been unbelievable,” she said.Allen completed 27 of 45 passes for 304 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the win. The numbers show production, but the turnovers explain why his performance drew scrutiny.Chiefs defense could expose Josh Allen’s decision-making againKimes is not the only analyst concerned. Dan Orlovsky has also questioned Allen’s choices in recent weeks, including against the Jets and Dolphins.“I’ve been concerned about Josh Allen for a couple of weeks now… He did not play well against the Jets… Yesterday was probably the most concerning game that I’ve seen from Josh in two or three seasons… He threw two interceptions, and it could have been four,” Orlovsky said.Allen has thrown for 2,527 yards and 14 touchdowns this season, with nine interceptions. He has added 290 rushing yards and 11 rushing scores. Those numbers still make him one of the league’s most dangerous quarterbacks.Kansas City, however, presents a different challenge. Kimes expects defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo to test Buffalo’s receivers with man coverage and see whether Allen can punish the defense with his legs.“Now, you’re going up against a Chiefs defense that isn’t going to give you the easy stuff. I’m interested in seeing how aggressively Spagnuolo plays this one. He’ll probably believe his DBs are better than the Bills’. The Chiefs’ defense, in man coverage, is fourth-best in the NFL. They only have 3.5 yards per attempt to tight ends. They’re second best against receivers,” she said.Buffalo will need Allen to take the available yards rather than force a big play on every possession. Against a defense that limits easy completions, patience could be just as valuable as his arm strength.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rams TE Tyler Higbee ruled out of Week 12 with a chest injury
articles.summary: The Rams lost two tight ends to injury in Week 12, including veteran Tyler Higbee.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams got hit with two big injuries at the tight end position in Week 12 against the Green Bay Packers . After Davis Allen was ruled out of the game in the second half with an ankle injury , veteran tight end Tyler Higbee sustained a chest injury that forced him out of the game, too.

It's unclear when the injury occurred, but the loss means the only tight ends the Rams have at the moment are Colby Parkinson and rookie Max Klare. Terrence Ferguson was ruled out for the remainder of the season with an ankle injury before Week 12.

This has been an unfortunate trend for the Rams' offense this year that already lost Puka Nacua for the year and Davante Adams earlier in the season. Adams should return from his hamstring injury, but his timeline is uncertain .

Before the injury, Higbee had caught one pass for 14 yards. He has 31 receptions for 304 yards and two touchdowns this year.

articles.title: Kyle Shanahan names 49ers new starting right tackle
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers didn't take long to name a new starter after RT Colton McKivitz suffered a season-ending injury.
articles.body:
It didn't take long for San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan to name a starting right tackle to replace Colton McKivitz who suffered a gruesome, season-ending ankle injury in Week 11.

Veteran offensive lineman Vederian Lowe, who was brought in to be the team's swing tackle, filled in admirably for the final two-and-a-half quarters of Sunday night's game against the Minnesota Vikings . That was enough for Shanahan to quickly give him the nod ahead of Week 12.

"I thought he played real well," Shanahan said. "Coming in, especially going against that defense, just all the problems that they present, so I thought he came in and stepped it up really well. That's why we brought him here. Anytime you have a swing tackle, that means you better be capable of starting. He's started a lot of games in this league and has played like a starter and that's why we targeted him as a swing tackle."

Lowe has played in 56 games as a pro with 25 starts. Four of those 25 starts came at right tackle for the New England Patriots in 2023. The other 21 starts came at left tackle. Sunday was his first real offensive action with the 49ers. He played in 38 offensive snaps, which eclipsed the 36 total he played across the first 10 weeks. His previous high in snaps with the 49ers was 22 in a Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

For Shanahan the choice probably wasn't difficult in part because there are no healthy options. Rookie Enrique Cruz Jr. continues to pile up healthy scratches, and veteran Austen Pleasants has been on IR all year nursing a knee injury he sustained in the offseason. Pleasants on Wednesday had his 21-day practice window opened , but it sounds like he's in line to step back into the swing tackle role he occupied a season ago while Lowe steps in as the No. 1 right tackle.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Reacts to Brandon Aiyuk's Commanders Contract, Talks Relationship After WR's Posts
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels made it clear that he is "happy" to reunite with receiver Brandon Aiyuk, a teammate from his college days at Arizona State.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels made it clear that he is "happy" to reunite with receiver Brandon Aiyuk, a teammate from his college days at Arizona State.

Aiyuk is signing a practice squad with the Commanders after being released by the San Francisco 49ers after a tumultuous offseason. Now, Daniels is looking forward to getting the opportunity to play with the wideout again.

Aiyuk made news after calling out Daniels in offseason posts . However, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported last week that Aiyuk "reached out to Daniels about a month ago to reconcile."

Daniels confirmed the two are on good terms on Wednesday:

That's good news for Commanders fans, as they will need the pair to have a good connection if the team wants to make a run at the playoffs.

Earlier this season, Daniels returned from his dislocated left elbow in Week 5 against the New York Giants, albeit with a sizable brace on his left arm.

The 2024 Pro Bowler received the necessary approvals to get back on the field. Still, his decision to put off surgery and only miss two games raised obvious concerns.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Oct. 11 that "there are doctors around the league who, despite not having examined Daniels, maintain that a player who dislocates his elbow twice — as Daniels has over the past 11 months — is at a higher risk suffering another dislocation, according to sources."

While Washington (4-5-1) remains in third place in the NFC East, the team has started to pick up momentum. It has won three of its past four games to get within two games of the first-place New York Giants.

Now, the Commanders are hoping Aiyuk can get up to speed quickly and re-establish a connection with Daniels to try to help the team make a run.

articles.title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026-27, Standings, Bracket Scenarios After Rams Beat Packers
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams used Wednesday night's win over the Green Bay Packers to leap into a playoff position in the NFC.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams used Wednesday night's win over the Green Bay Packers to leap into a playoff position in the NFC.

Matthew Stafford and Co. knocked off the Packers by a 26-13 score to move up to 7-4.

The Rams have a long road ahead of them to maintain a spot in the top seven of the NFC. That road includes a pair of games against the Seattle Seahawks, who are directly beneath them in the standings.

Green Bay fell out of the playoff places with the loss, but the good news for the Packers is that they play four of their last five games at Lambeau Field.

Two of the three games on Thanksgiving Day carry massive playoff implications.

The Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears play for first place in the NFC North, while the Kansas City Chiefs visit the Buffalo Bills in a game that will play a big role in the race for home-field advantage.

The renewal of the Buffalo-Kansas City rivalry take center stage on Thanksgiving night.

Thursday's game is one of two massive holiday clashes for the Bills this year. They also visit the Denver Broncos on Christmas Day.

Buffalo plays four of its last seven games on the road, including trips to New England and Green Bay, so a win at home over a conference rival would be huge.

Kansas City can't afford a loss either since it is locked in a tight divisional race with the Broncos. The AFC West rivals split their regular-season series.

Denver appears to have an easy win on its hands on Friday against the Pittsburgh Steelers, who cut Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday.

Mason Rudolph is a significant drop down in talent from Rodgers. The assumption is the Steelers will fall out of the entire playoff discussion in the coming weeks.

Pittsburgh's sudden quarterback change will shake up the wild-card race. The Steelers currently own the No. 7 seed.

The Houston Texans' Sunday clash with the Baltimore Ravens now carries more weight with Pittsburgh in chaos and the Las Vegas Raiders on the road in Cleveland.

Houston has a favorable schedule, which includes Pittsburgh in Week 13, that could allow it to claw back into the No. 7 seed.

The Los Angeles Rams jumped up into the final wild-card position with Wednesday's win over the Green Bay Packers.

There's a chance the Rams stay at the No. 7 seed for the rest of the weekend. That would happen if the Seattle Seahawks lose on the road to the San Francisco 49ers on Saturday afternoon.

Regardless of what happens on Sunday, the Rams and Seahawks will be locked into the battle for a playoff spot for most of the rest of the regular season. The NFC West rivals meet in Weeks 16 and 18.

Green Bay is the only NFC North team outside of the playoff places after Wednesday.

The NFC North lead is up for grabs on Thanksgiving Day, as the Detroit Lions host the Chicago Bears.

Detroit sits in first place right now on the division record tiebreaker. Thursday is the first of two meetings between the Bears and Lions. They also square off in Chicago in Week 17.

The Dallas Cowboys can't move into any playoff position on Thanksgiving, but they can put some pressure on the New York Giants atop the NFC East with a win over the Philadelphia Eagles.

Dallas needs to keep winning and receive help from the Giants' opponents to claw back into a playoff position.

articles.title: Micah Returns in Packers' Loss to Rams, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Stafford, Love, Top Players
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams continue to win even with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams sidelined.
articles.body:
Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams continue to win even with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams sidelined.

Los Angeles extended its winning streak to five with a 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers in Wednesday's NFC showdown at SoFi Stadium. It is now 7-4 on the season and moved ahead of the 6-5 Packers in the NFC standings.

While Micah Parsons returned for the first time this season after he was sidelined while recovering from a torn ACL, he and the Green Bay defense failed to contain Blake Corum and the dominant Rams rushing attack.

It also didn't help the visitors that Jordan Love and the offense failed to score a single point in the second half.

Parsons' return was far from the only major storyline, as both teams were tied with the Seattle Seahawks in the race for the final NFC wild-card spot entering play. That made this a critical swing game with the victor earning the head-to-head tiebreaker, so it was fitting it started in back-and-forth fashion.

Los Angeles seized the initial momentum despite settling for multiple field goals. Tucker Kraft lost a fumble on one end, while Kyren Williams found paydirt in the second quarter for the game's first touchdown on the other. Williams scored, but it was set up by Stafford spreading the ball around and finding Konata Mumpfield and Tyler Higbee.

However, Green Bay answered right back when Love found Watson for a touchdown after their previous connection on a trick play and a long completion to Matthew Golden.

That wasn't even the most notable play in the first half involving Watson, though, as he was on the receiving end of a hard hit from Kamren Kinchens. Kinchens was ejected, while the go-to receiver was ruled out with a concussion.

While the injury was a concern, the Packers still took momentum into the second half after Parsons brought down Stafford for his first sack of the season.

But momentum can only go so far when the offense drastically changes without its go-to receiver, and that's exactly what happened for Green Bay without Watson available to beat defenders over the top with his speed and create openings for his teammates.

The offense did nothing for the majority of the second half, including when Love threw a terrible interception to Jaylen McCollough from promising field position following Stafford's interception to Ty'Ron Hopper.

With their primary receivers missing and Green Bay struggling on the other end, the Rams turned to the rushing attack to take the lead in the third quarter. It took Corum four attempts inside the 5-yard line, but he finally punched it in and set the tone for a physical second half as Los Angeles continued to run the ball and control the clock.

The worn-down Packers defense eventually allowed Corum to break through for a 35-yard run while the Rams were salting the game away to set up the field goal that extended the lead to double digits.

By the time Love threw yet another interception, this time to Emmanuel Forbes Jr., the game was all but over.

The Rams will now put their winning streak on the line for a high-profile home game against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs, while the Packers will look to bounce back on the road against the New Orleans Saints.

articles.title: 2026 NFL Week 12 Biggest Takeaways for Every Team
articles.summary: Thanksgiving week has arrived. For football fans, that means a week stuffed with NFL action. For the teams taking the field between Wednesday and Monday, it's time to fight for the final stretch.
articles.body:
Thanksgiving week has arrived. For football fans, that means a week stuffed with NFL action. For the teams taking the field between Wednesday and Monday, it's time to fight for the final stretch.

Nobody can clinch a playoff berth this week. Starting in Week 13, though, some teams could punch their tickets and others could see their seasons end.

This week's action began with a special Thanksgiving Eve game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams. Things will pick back up on Thursday with a traditional three-game Thanksgiving slate.

Bleacher Report analysts Brad Gagnon , Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will follow the action throughout the week to break down the biggest stories and most pressing questions emerging from each contest.

The Rams have lost Puka Nacua to a season-ending knee injury, and Davante Adams remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. Unsurprisingly, Sean McVay drew up a run-heavy game plan against the Packers on Wednesday night. What might concern future opponents is the fact that the plan worked to near-perfection.

Kyren Williams has been battling turf toe, so it was a heavy workload for Blake Corum. He repeatedly battered the Packers and finished with 184 yards and a touchdown on 34 carries. As a team, the Rams finished with 241 rushing yards.

By wearing down Green Bay's defense, keeping its own defense off the field, and relying on its stellar pass rush to force mistakes, Los Angeles took full control of the game after halftime. It's a strategy that should keep the Rams in the playoff mix until Adams returns and/or other pass-catchers prove to be reliable targets for Matthew Stafford.

How Many Injuries Can Los Angeles Endure?

The injuries at receiver have been well-documented. If the Rams are going to take a run-heavy approach for the foreseeable future, it would help to have healthy blockers up front. Unfortunately, they're running out of those, too.

Guard Steve Avila and center Coleman Shelton both missed Wednesday's game with injuries. Guard Bill Murray left the game with an injury, as did tight ends Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee.

With games against the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers upcoming, L.A. could desperately use some good news on the injury front soon.

The Packers' Inability To Run Effectively Is a Fatal Flaw

The Packers managed to keep things close in the first half and took a 13-13 tie into halftime. However, their passing offense stalled significantly when Christian Watson exited with a concussion. Green Bay never regained momentum, in part, because it just couldn't run the ball and sustain drives.

The Packers rushed for just 55 yards and possessed the ball for just over 19 minutes. Quarterback Jordan Love was forced to carry the offense with a limited number of possessions, and he was picked off twice.

It's worth noting that Green Bay didn't have starting back Josh Jacobs, who is out with a finger injury. However, the inability to run efficiently is not a new issue for the Packers, who came into Week 12 ranked 32nd in yards per carry and rushing yards.

How Can Green Bay Improve Its Offensive Line?

The Packers' ground game has struggled largely because the offensive line hasn't regularly opened running lanes up front. That trend continued against Los Angeles, and guard Kevin Zeitler exited with an ankle injury and didn't return.

Love was only sacked once, but he was pressured into two turnovers and rarely had time to attack downfield.

At 6-5, Green Bay is now in danger of sliding out of the wild-card picture. The Packers have to figure out how to be better up front if they're going to salvage their season. That's easier in theory than in practice, of course, but the status quo isn't working.

A Buccaneers win in the rematch could spark a run to the top of the division, while a Panthers victory could allow Carolina to run away with the NFC South.

articles.title: NFL Thanksgiving Day preview: Eagles QB Joe Milton hopes to spoil Cowboys' hopes in his old home
articles.summary: Joe Milton spent parts of the past two seasons in Dallas. Now he's headed back to take on the desperate Cowboys in the middle game on Thanksgiving.
articles.body:
The middle game of the Thanksgiving trio — the stuffing, if you will — lacks the meat and potatoes of the first and final games of the day. But Eagles at Cowboys still carries some potential playoff importance.

The 5-6 Cowboys host the 3-7 Eagles in a game that matters to Dallas. The Cowboys' offense has hit its stride recently, scoring 40 and 51 points, respectively, the past two games. Over the past five games, Dallas hasn't scored fewer than 27.

The problem? They're only 3-2 in that stretch, and the NFC East-leading Giants have kept that same pace.

The other problem? Dallas' defense. There were modest signs of improvement on that side of the ball in Mike Pettine's first game calling plays, especially compared to how the defense played against the 49ers. And for the first game possibly all season, the Cowboys could make a strong claim that they had the better defense — the Titans are that bad now, yes.

The Eagles limped into the bye with seven straight losses, but they're coming off one of their best efforts of the season in beating the Steelers on Sunday. Defensively, they kept the Steelers under wraps for most of the four quarters and gave QB Joe Milton and the offense a chance.

Milton returns to Dallas, where he spent parts of the past two seasons and saw action in four games last season behind Dak Prescott. Now Milton gets a chance to take on his former QB1 on Thursday after signing with the Eagles after Jalen Hurts landed on injured reserve.

The Cowboys left Milton, a preseason star the past two years, unprotected on their practice squad, and the Eagles gladly scooped him up. He has a chance to make the Cowboys pay for letting him walk — and before one of the biggest TV audiences Milton might have.

The Eagles' playoff hopes hover at less than 1%, according to Next Gen Stats . The Cowboys, however, are still alive at 22%, barely above the Commanders (21%) and behind the Giants (65%).

A loss would be pretty devastating. But beating Philadelphia would give the Cowboys a 3-1 mark in the division, which is the one edge they have right now on the Giants, who are 2-1-1 in NFC East games. The East could come down to the Week 17 Giants-Cowboys game, but every divisional matchup counts.

The Eagles, however, didn't look like a team ready to mail it in on Sunday. They showed some renewed vitality after the bye, with the team giving some younger players opportunities to stand out, including Milton. For Milton, there's personal pride on the line after spending parts of the past two years in Dallas, facing a defense that has plenty to prove.

When the Eagles traded Jordan Davis to the Jaguars, it shone the spotlight more on Jalen Carter, who started this season slowly but whose play has been on the rise lately. In Sunday's upset of the Steelers, Carter was active and effective despite suffering a quad injury just prior to the game. He was a full participant in practice this week, but the player he might have faced off against, Cowboys right guard Tyler Booker, did not practice and is not expected to play Thursday. The Eagles know they have to slow down Dallas' passing attack and pressure Dak Prescott, and the best way to do that might be to detonate the operation from the inside. Carter and the Eagles also can't have a repeat of the last meeting, in Week 7, when Dallas ran for 204 yards on 38 carries.

Sportsbooks opened this game Cowboys -1.5 in the summer — now it's -8.5. Losing Jalen Hurts for the season, along with a 3-7 record (and a putrid 2-8 record against the spread) will do that. Philadelphia put up a spirited defensive effort in a 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers as 3.5-point home underdogs on Sunday, but this Dallas offense will provide a much stiffer test. Eagles starting QB Joe Milton and Philadelphia collected only 11 first downs and 214 yards of total offense; that's not going to get it done. Dak Prescott & Co. can't control how well a rejuvenated defense plays under Mike Pettine, but the Cowboys have scored at least 27 points in each of the past five games. Dallas scored 51 points against Tennessee on Sunday; the Eagles have scored 40 points combined in their past three contests. The Eagles D will put up a good fight, but barring several turnovers, I don't believe it will be able to keep up with Dallas. Cowboys -2.5 is another good teaser leg to go with that Packers +8.5, which cashed on Wednesday. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

We always expect plentiful points in any Dallas game, even with a struggling Philadelphia offense on the other side. Here are three fantasy themes to track as you watch the middle of the three Thanksgiving games.

1. What version of Saquon Barkley do we see? Barkley is expected to play despite a neck injury, but he hasn't been a high-volume back in 2026. Last week's 17 touches against the Steelers were actually his high for the year, which tells you a lot about Philly's season. This is also the worst Philadelphia offensive line in several years.

2. How involved will George Pickens be? Dallas seemed to lose the plot with Pickens a few weeks ago, sending him just 10 targets over a two-week period (including a 4-57-1 game against Philadelphia). Since then, Dak Prescott has peppered both Pickens and CeeDee Lamb, and the Cowboys have scored 91 points over two weeks. Several teams in the NFL employ wide usage trees. Dallas doesn't want to be one of them.

3. Is DeVonta Smith ready to pop? Smith saw plenty of opportunity in the win over Pittsburgh (12 targets), though he returned a modest 5-41-0 line. The Eagles have a capped ceiling with Joe Milton at quarterback, but at least they're trying to get Smith going. Dallas' secondary has been torched for most of the season. — Scott Pianowski

articles.title: NFL: Los Angeles Rams beat Green Bay Packers 26-13 in Thanksgiving Eve clash for fifth straight win in playoff push
articles.summary: Blake Corum led Los Angeles Rams' dominant rushing attack as they beat Green Bay Packers 26-13; Rams are on a five-game winning streak as the Packers suffered their second successive loss; watch the NFL's Thanksgiving triple-header live on Sky Sports from 5pm on Thursday
articles.body:
Blake Corum rushed for a career-high 184 yards and a touchdown, while Kyren Williams ran for another score, as the Rams (7-4) got stellar efforts from their rushing attack and a stout defense to stay firmly in the NFC playoff race.

Corum extended his breakout season with another impressive outing on his 26th birthday, scoring a TD in his seventh consecutive game. Green Bay (6-5) have lost two straight for the first time since losing their final five games last season.

"What you learn is, every single week you've got to adjust and adapt," Rams coach Sean McVay said. "The game honors toughness, and I think we're playing tougher. We're learning how to establish possession."

Los Angeles controlled the ball for 23:45 in the second half, squeezing the life from the Packers inside a lively SoFi Stadium for their Thanksgiving Eve match-up.

The Rams did it behind Corum, whose 32 carries were the most in the NFL this season and the most by any Rams running back in McVay's 10-year career. Corum had 25 carries for 161 yards in the second half alone while Los Angeles stayed in control.

"We knew coming in that we would have to be a physical team, and I think we were the more physical team tonight," Corum said.

Jordan Love passed for 198 yards with two interceptions for Green Bay, who only had the ball for 19:20 - just 6:15 in the second half - in a loss that pushed it farther from play-off contention.

Christian Watson had four catches for 65 yards and an early touchdown, but the star receiver was ruled out just before half-time with a concussion on a hard hit from Rams safety Kam Kinchens, who was ejected .

"Losing the turnover battle, and then on top of that, our inability to stop the run - which is exactly what we knew they were going to do - that was a recipe for disaster, and tonight it was," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said.

Micah Parsons had a sack in his season debut, but Green Bay's defense couldn't thwart the Rams' methodical ground attack.

Rams continue winning run despite star absentees

McVay has changed his offense's focus with star receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both injured for the past two games.

NFL MVP Matthew Stafford passed for just 140 yards against the Packers, while LA ran the ball 47 times despite losing two starters in the second half from an offensive line that was already down two previous starters.

Brandon McManus also kicked four field goals against his former team for the Rams, who snapped their five-game skid in their rivalry with the Packers. McVay finally earned his first victory over LaFleur, his offensive coordinator in Los Angeles in his debut season in 2017.

Rams linebacker Nate Landman produced his fourth forced fumble of the season on the Packers' second drive, leading to Los Angeles' second field goal. Williams scored from seven yards out early in the second quarter, giving the Rams points on their first three drives for the first time all season.

Green Bay responded with a confident 80-yard drive for Watson's short TD catch, but Watson was injured on Kinchens' hit shortly before halftime.

After the Rams made a 14-play drive out of halftime ending with Corum's one-yard TD plunge, they were rolling downfield again until Ty'Ron Hopper picked off Stafford's underthrown pass - but, two plays later, Jaylen McCollough intercepted Love's inaccurate throw to the goal line.

articles.title: Meet Mason Rudolph: 31-year-old NFL quarterback replacing Aaron Rodgers as he returns to the Pittsburgh Steelers’ starting role after winning three consecutive games in 2023
articles.summary: Mason Rudolph is back in the spotlight after the Pittsburgh Steelers named him their starting quarterback for the upcoming game against the Denver
articles.body: Mason Rudolph is back in the spotlight after the Pittsburgh Steelers named him their starting quarterback for the upcoming game against the Denver Broncos, meaning Aaron Rodgers will remain on the bench. The decision, announced Nov. 24, 2026, has put the spotlight on a player who has spent much of his pro career waiting for chances, rather than a regular spot in the lineup. Now 31, Rudolph returns to a familiar role with Pittsburgh, carrying the experience of several seasons marked by competition, setbacks and occasional breakthroughs.Who is Mason Rudolph, the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterbackRudolph is an American professional football quarterback who plays for the Pittsburgh Steelers in the National Football League. Standing 6 feet 5 inches tall and weighing 235 pounds, he attended Oklahoma State University before entering the NFL. According to his official player profile on the NFL website, he has nine years of professional experience and wears jersey number 2 for Pittsburgh.The Steelers selected Rudolph in the third round of the 2018 NFL Draft. His arrival, however, did not immediately establish him as the team's future starting quarterback. The Associated Press reported that the selection raised eyebrows at the time, particularly because the franchise already had an established quarterback in Ben Roethlisberger. Former general manager Kevin Colbert had valued Rudolph highly, with the team reportedly grading him as a first-round talent.A promising start followed by difficult seasonsRudolph's early years in Pittsburgh involved competing for opportunities in a team where the starting position was difficult to secure. He made his NFL debut in the second week of the 2019 season against Seattle and became a starter the following week against San Francisco.His first significant opportunity came in 2019 when Roethlisberger was recovering from right elbow surgery. Rudolph finished that season with a 5-3 record as a starter, throwing 13 touchdown passes and nine interceptions, according to AP. However, inconsistency affected his performances, and head coach Mike Tomlin eventually replaced him with Devlin Hodges.His time in Pittsburgh also featured a tough moment in 2019 when he was part of a highly publicized on-field clash with Cleveland Browns player Myles Garrett. The Associated Press reported the incident as one of the downs in Rudolph's early NFL career, which has had its ups and downs. But he kept working in the team and was there when opportunities came.The 2023 season brought a breakthroughOne of Rudolph's most important career moments came towards the end of the 2023 regular season. After spending considerable time outside the starting line-up, he returned to the field and helped Pittsburgh win 3 consecutive games to close the campaign.According to the Steelers' official player statistics, those victories included important away wins against Seattle and Baltimore. His performance against Baltimore in the final regular-season game was particularly notable. Rudolph completed 18 of his 20 passing attempts for 152 yards and a touchdown, recording a passer rating of 115.0.His 90% completion rate in that game became the best single-game completion percentage in Steelers franchise history among performances with at least 20 passing attempts. The three victories also helped Pittsburgh qualify for the playoffs.However, the team could not continue its winning run in the postseason. The Steelers lost 31-17 to the Buffalo Bills in the AFC wild-card round. Although the campaign gave Rudolph a chance to demonstrate his abilities, it did not secure him a permanent starting position.From Pittsburgh to Tennessee and back againThe Steelers released Rudolph following the 2023 season, moving on from him as their starting quarterback. Russell Wilson signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Rudolph signed with the Tennessee Titans.His time in Tennessee provided another opportunity to play regularly. According to his official Steelers career statistics, he appeared in eight regular-season games for the Titans, making five starts. He completed 146 of 228 passing attempts for 1,530 yards and nine touchdowns.Rudolph returned to Pittsburgh in 2025 and became part of the team's quarterback group again. He played in 5 regular-season games that year, including one start, recording 310 passing yards and two touchdowns, according to the Steelers' official statistics.His return meant another period of competing for playing time. With Rodgers occupying the starting position, Rudolph largely remained a backup, waiting for the possibility of being called upon.Another opportunity puts Mason Rudolph in focusThe latest change in Pittsburgh has given Rudolph another chance to lead the team. The Steelers officially confirmed the decision through a statement from team spokesman Burt Lauten on November 24, 2026. The announcement said Rudolph would start against Denver on Friday, November 27, while Rodgers would be inactive for the game.According to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, the decision followed the team's offensive struggles in its previous two games against the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles. A team source told the newspaper that Pittsburgh believed Rudolph could provide the spark needed to improve its performances. The report also clarified that the change initially applies only to the Denver game, with the quarterback situation to be reviewed afterwards.Rudolph enters the opportunity with an NFL starting record of nine wins, nine losses and one tie. The Steelers' official statistics show that eight of those victories came during his time as a Pittsburgh starter, where his record stands at 8-5-1.For a player who has spent several seasons waiting behind more established names, the latest decision represents another important moment in his career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: Después de ser relegado al banquillo el martes, el jugador fue finalmente despedido de los Pittsburgh por criticar a su entrenador en una entrevista
articles.summary: Después de ser relegado al banquillo el martes, el jugador fue finalmente despedido de los Pittsburgh por criticar a su entrenador en una entrevista
articles.body: Los Pittsburgh Steelers han despedido al legendario jugador Aaron Rodgers, horas después de que el cuatro veces MVP de la NFL acusara al entrenador en jefe, Mike McCarthy, de quedarse dormido durante las reuniones del equipo. Rodgers hizo estas acusaciones durante una inesperada intervención de más de media hora en un programa de la cadena ESPN, 'The Pat McAfee Show', después de que los Steelers lo hubieran relegado al banquillo en favor del quarterback suplente Mason Rudolph. El jugador, de 42 años, acusó a McCarthy de quedarse dormido y roncar con frecuencia en las citas con el equipo, además de faltar a algunas de ellas. Tras estas críticas, el equipo anunció que rescindían el contrato de Rodgers. “El miércoles pasado estábamos en una reunión. Mike llegó tarde, se sentó y, a los diez minutos, empezó a roncar. Se despertó solo, haciendo ruido con sus papeles”, dijo Rodgers en esta entrevista. “Todos nos miramos. Cinco minutos después, se oyeron los ronquidos otra vez. Y menos de cinco minutos después, salió de la sala como si nada hubiera pasado”. “Hemos liberado al quarterback Aaron Rodgers”, escribieron en redes sociales los Steelers, que han perdido sus dos últimos partidos, aunque aún se aferran al último puesto de playoffs en la AFC. McCarthy confirmó que fue su decisión dejar en el banquillo a Aaron. Y sobre el hecho de que cerrara su arenga en el descanso del encuentro con el grito "¡1, 2, 3 Packers!", el técnico explicó que "fue un momento muy emocional y hubo conversaciones antes de eso. Resultó un momento vergonzoso, pero creo que trabajamos muchísimas horas". Si ningún otro equipo reclama a Rodgers en la lista de transferibles, se convertirá en agente libre sin restricciones. Hay varios equipos, como los Indianapolis Colts y los New England Patriots, que necesitan un quarterback titular en este momento. Seleccionado en el draft de 2005 por los Green Bay Packers, Rodgers se convirtió en titular tres años después y llevó al equipo a la victoria en la Super Bowl de 2011.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers’ strange NFL trip may be over. The incendiary final act is a fitting last chapter
articles.summary: As Aaron Rodgers tore into his former head coach on live television, his headphone mic incessantly brushing up against his sweatshirt, he appeared to be a man at peace with ending a glittering NFL career.
articles.body: As Aaron Rodgers tore into his head coach on live television, his headphone mic incessantly brushing up against his sweatshirt, he appeared to be a man at peace with ending a glittering NFL career. Rodgers was once the golden boy in Green Bay, a four-time MVP and Super Bowl champion. He dated movie stars, made the “Discount Double Check” a meme in State Farm ads, and was known as one of the most charismatic off-the-field characters in the league. He appears set to leave the stage as one of the most baffling personalities in recent NFL history, torching Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy on “The Pat McAfee Show,” the same platform where he became known for Covid-19 skepticism, anti-vaccination takes, political rants and general grumpiness that made those halcyon days in Wisconsin feel very far in the past. From the moment the Steelers revealed Rodgers would be benched for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos, the NFL world readied itself for the quarterback’s response. In fact, most everyone expected him to pop up on McAfee’s show, a place where he regularly appeared before his penchant for getting off hot takes became the worst thing in football: a “distraction.” But no one quite expected the level Rodgers was ready to go to when he finally popped up on air. Within about two minutes, he had accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings, skipping other meetings, not watching game film, questioning his health and alleging that his coach had mistakenly referred to the Steelers as the Packers when breaking a huddle at halftime. “Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring,” Rodgers said. “Woke himself up, was rattling his papers, we all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again and less than five minutes after that he walks out the room like nothing happened.” Rodgers said the head coach was then absent from an offensive meeting on Thursday before failing to show at a walkthrough on Friday and missing a morning meeting on Saturday before the Steelers’ game in Philadelphia. It was during Sunday’s game against the Eagles that Rodgers said McCarthy lost a lot of the team. “I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime, towards the end of it … there’s some rambling or something and without even a heads- up he says, ‘Alright, 1, 2, 3, Packers,’” Rodgers said. “That’s what he broke it down on in the locker room.” In the lengthy interview, which was mostly a Rodgers monologue broken up by McAfee trying to wrap his head around what he was hearing, the quarterback also accused McCarthy of not taking game planning seriously, not watching enough film, not being as all-in as other high-level NFL head coaches and not really speaking with anyone on the defensive side of the ball. Complaints about how he was treated were expected. Pulling back the curtain on the Steelers’ 2026 season and setting fire to McCarthy’s reputation? Certainly not. A long time coming In a way, the last five years of Rodgers’ career all built to this moment. There is a through line from the moment that he told the media in 2021 that he was “immunized” against Covid-19 – a time when vaccinations were mandatory to play – to his appearance on McAfee on Wednesday. There was the revelation that he was taking ayahuasca as part of his off-season preparations, an admission of drug use that likely wouldn’t fly for just about anyone else. His darkness retreat in 2023, when he was considering whether to retire. The repeated public criticisms of teammates in Green Bay and New York after he moved to the Jets. A feud with Jimmy Kimmel that ended with Rodgers insinuating a non-existent link between the comedian and Jeffrey Epstein. The flirtation with retiring from football to serve as Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s running mate. And, of course, his on-field remonstrations toward McCarthy this year. His prodigious talent allowed him to get away with a lot that teams would not have put up with if he had a lesser résumé. And, when he was benched in Pittsburgh, Rodgers became – in his own words – someone “with nothing to lose.” And, as he did so often on the field, Rodgers aired it all out. But this time, it’s different. Rodgers is no longer that time-defying MVP who is carrying his team to victories. He’s much more limited on the field ever since his 2023 Achilles injury. He’s clearly regressed from last season’s AFC North-winning campaign for the Steelers. Part of that isn’t his fault; he’s spent a lot of time on the turf as a leaky offensive line allows pass rushers in. There are a few possible landing spots for the last few months of Rodgers’ career, which he has said will be over after this season. The New England Patriots are in the hunt and Drake Maye is out for the season with a broken ankle. The Baltimore Ravens and Indianapolis Colts are also facing QB troubles, even though they are largely out of the playoff race. What comes next? Even if any of those teams wanted to bring in a new signal-caller to try and improve their offense for the last two months of the regular season, the real question is this: Does anyone want to deal with a guy who just tore apart his last coach? Quarterbacks are looked at as the ultimate leaders in American sports. They are the faces of their franchises, the person everyone on the roster looks to for inspiration in big moments. It’s an outsized job, a level of pressure that is unmatched in the rest of major American sports. A football team needs to have absolute faith in its quarterback in order to be successful. And maybe that’s what Rodgers thought he was doing. Maybe, in tossing a Molotov cocktail into McCarthy’s already-shaky reputation, he thought he was doing one last solid for the Steelers on the way out the door. It does seem that something is amiss in Pittsburgh. Local reporters were quick to confirm strife behind the scenes in the Steel City and parts of Rodgers’ tirade were immediately corroborated by unnamed team sources – including the damning allegation of McCarthy falling asleep in a meeting. McCarthy himself didn’t exactly launch a vigorous self-defense in his postgame press conference, declining to discuss private conversations (though he did appear to confirm that he said “Packers” instead of Steelers on Sunday). He also seemed to confirm the reason why Rodgers was benched in the first place. The quarterback told McAfee that he had met with McCarthy and detailed his problems with the coach before Rodgers demanded the head coach either give up playcalling duties or cut him. McCarthy made clear on Wednesday that the decision was his. The Pittsburgh coach is about to lead his 11th game as the man in charge of his hometown team. He now faces the task of proving Rodgers wrong about his work ethic, his health, his knowledge of the game and his preparation for each week. McCarthy won a Super Bowl with Rodgers in Green Bay and together they had many successful years, but he couldn’t get back to that mountaintop – either with Rodgers in Green Bay or without him during his years in Dallas. Now, he’s got Mason Rudolph under center as he tries to salvage a season that seems to have just had the bottom fall out. Rodgers’ legacy If the Steelers do fall apart and McCarthy’s reputation flounders further, it’s possible Rodgers will be proven right. But at what cost? In January 2023, Rodgers’ Packers were defeated on “Sunday Night Football” by the Detroit Lions, ruining their playoff hopes in the final game of the regular season. Lions safety Kerby Joseph picked him off on his final pass and Rodgers left Lambeau Field for the last time, hanging his head. He had just turned 39. His successor, Jordan Love, was waiting in the wings. The Packers appeared ready to turn the page and so did he. If that was the moment Rodgers chose to hang up his cleats, he would have left the league a legend who retired near the top of his game, still making incredible throws with his cannon of a right arm. He would have gone down as a successful quarterback who would always be more known for what he did on the field instead of the controversies he embraced in the last couple of years of his career. Instead, he appears set to exit the stage as a human torch, setting fire to a season that was in the throes of a playoff push and leaving his former teammates to pick up the pieces. It’s now possible that the final image of Rodgers as an active NFL player won’t be in uniform, tossing a late-game touchdown on Sunday with a signature bit of scrambling and deft touch. Instead, it will be of him on a webcam, unburdening himself to a baffled Pat McAfee and a stoic AJ Hawk. It seems, sadly, a fitting ending.
