articles.title: Aaron Rodgers’ NFL future takes another turn as three teams emerge as potential destinations for the veteran quarterback
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers waived Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday, hours after he gave a blistering interview on the Pat McAfee Show about coach Mike McCarthy.
articles.body: The Pittsburgh Steelers waived Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday, hours after he gave a blistering interview on the Pat McAfee Show about coach Mike McCarthy. The move came a day after Pittsburgh named Mason Rudolph its starter for the Black Friday game against the Broncos. Rodgers, 42, has said he will retire after this season. The trade deadline has passed, so any team can claim him off waivers until 4 p.m. ET Thursday. If nobody does, he becomes a free agent. The Cardinals, Ravens and Patriots each have a reason to at least make a call.Aaron Rodgers' NFL future depends on one waiver windowRodgers is not arriving with a hot hand. He has completed 60.9% of his passes this year, with 16 touchdowns, six interceptions and a career-low passer rating of 86.6. The season still has more than a month left, though, and plenty of teams are playing quarterbacks they never planned to use.His retirement plan changes the math too. Nobody is signing him for the long term. A claim would be a short rental, and the only question is whether a team believes he makes its next few weeks better.Arizona is the longest shot, but it has the most familiar faces. The Cardinals are 3-8 and well out of the playoff race. Head coach Mike LaFleur is the younger brother of Matt LaFleur, who coached Rodgers in Green Bay for four seasons. Offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett worked with Rodgers in Green Bay from 2019 to 2021, in the same role he holds now, and again with the Jets in 2023 and 2024.The quarterback room is a mess. Jacoby Brissett started the year, lost the job to Gardner Minshew, and then Minshew and rookie Carson Beck both got hurt. That left journeyman Josh Johnson under center in Week 11 against the Chiefs.Nobody should call this likely. But the connections are real.Ravens and Patriots have the stronger football reasonsBaltimore would be the most entertaining fit. The Ravens are 4-7 and have lost six straight, yet they still sit in the AFC wild-card mix. They also play the Steelers twice, in Weeks 15 and 18. Rodgers would get two shots at the team that just cut him loose.The need is there as well. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both went down earlier this year. Baltimore started undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano in Week 9, then traded for Brissett from Arizona. So far that has not worked. Brissett is 0-2 with two interceptions.New England is the trickiest case. The Patriots are 5-5 and just outside the wild-card race. Drake Maye is out for the foreseeable future with a fractured fibula he suffered in Week 10, and coach Mike Vrabel has said Tommy DeVito will start until Maye returns.The relationship is awkward. Rodgers was a loud critic of Vrabel's offseason controversy involving reporter Dianna Russini, and that is hard to wave away. Then again, the Patriots reached the Super Bowl last season and are now fighting just to stay afloat. Signing Rodgers would also give him a chance to help keep the Steelers out of the postseason.There is a personnel link as well. Eliot Wolf, New England's executive vice president of player personnel, overlapped with Rodgers in Green Bay for 13 seasons.The answer arrives at 4 p.m. ET Thursday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Micah Parsons' $1.3 million home purchase became more than a real estate deal; it fulfilled a childhood promise
articles.summary: Micah Parsons bought his mother a $1.3 million house in Parker, Texas, in his first summer with the Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body: Micah Parsons bought his mother a $1.3 million house in Parker, Texas, in his first summer with the Dallas Cowboys. He showed it off on Instagram on Saturday, July 17, 2021. He was 22. It was one of the first big moves of his pro career. Dallas had drafted him 12th overall that April, and his four-year rookie deal was worth about $17 million. Before the draft, Parsons had said he wanted a home for himself and his mother. The purchase checked that box, and it still says a lot about how he handles money.Micah Parsons buys his mother a $1.3 million home in ParkerThe post was short. Micah Parsons shared a picture of his mother, Sherese, on his back in front of the house. His caption read, "Welcome mom this. All for you."Parker is a quiet suburb northeast of Dallas, and the house was meant for a full household. A WFAA report cited by Candy's Dirt said there was space for Parsons, Sherese, his young son Malcolm and other family. The price looked big on paper. Against a signing bonus of about $9.8 million, it was manageable. Outlets differ slightly on the bonus figure, but the guaranteed money across the deal sat near $17 million.He was also a young father. Malcolm was born in May 2018, shortly before Micah turned 19, which gave the house a second job: stability for a three-year-old.The motive was clear long before closing. Ahead of the draft, he told BroBible, "I moved a lot when I was younger." He wanted one address for him and his mother, a place that belonged to them. He also wanted to clear her debt.Where Parsons comes from adds weight. He grew up in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, and the Dallas Morning News described a city where violence, drugs and prison cut short a lot of promising lives. Parsons got out, played at Penn State, and then did what he said he would.How the promise looks after the Packers tradeThe story took on new meaning in August 2025, when Dallas traded Parsons to the Green Bay Packers. The move followed a tense training camp in which Parsons had asked the Cowboys for a trade. He signed a four-year, $188 million contract, making him the highest-paid non-quarterback in NFL history. Dallas got two first-round picks and defensive tackle Kenny Clark. Reports split on how much is fully guaranteed, with $120 million and $136 million both in circulation, so the headline number is the safer one to use.Sports Illustrated read the deal as the next chapter of the same story: the 2021 house first, then a level of security that outlasts any single contract.Sherese has always been central to it. Parsons once told PennLive, "if we had a million more Shereses, the world would be OK."What stands out is the order of things. The promise came first and the money came later. Plenty of rookie spending stories start with the cash. This one started with a plan, and the plan did not change when the numbers got bigger.The Parker house cost $1.3 million. The Packers deal runs $188 million. Only one of those figures was on his list before the draft. He sold that home for an estimated $1.67 million (a $370,000 increase) following his move to Green Bay.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers NFL career seems over but three teams could consider quarterback as a late-season option
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers says "not how I thought it would end" as the Steelers cut him hours after his Pat McAfee Show interview, leaving his NFL future unclear.
articles.body: The claims Aaron Rodgers made about Mike McCarthy on national television Wednesday undoubtedly got him cut by the Pittsburgh Steelers and now the question that remains is whether they ended his NFL career. "Not how I thought it would end," Rodgers said on his now viral interview on the "Pat McAfee Show." Everyone agrees. AARON RODGERS NOT RETURNING TO STEELERS, SAYS MIKE MCCARTHY FALLS ASLEEP IN MEETINGS AND IS 'UNWELL' "... If that's his final ride, you know what I mean, it's probably not the most ideal way to go out," said Raiders pass rusher Maxx Crosby when told of the news. "You don't want to see anyone go out like this." Rodgers going scorched Earth on McCarthy turned off some executives around the league who shared their feelings with OutKick throughout the day Wednesday. But, interestingly, not everyone believes Rodgers effectively ended his own career because of what he said. Several executives said they expect "some team" will consider or have internal discussions about signing the soon-to-be 43-year-old quarterback if he clears waivers by Thursday's 4 p.m. deadline. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Rodgers being subject to waivers means any team can claim him by the deadline. Any team that claims Rodgers would have to pay him the remaining portion of his guaranteed salary, which is approximately $8.6 million. As a practical matter, no team will be claiming Rodgers unless it has an understanding he would report. And Rodgers isn't going to report just anywhere, especially not a losing team with nothing to play for. But if Rodgers goes unclaimed, he becomes a free agent able to sign with any team he chooses, and he might be tempted to play if a team interests him. Then the intrigue would begin. While most teams will not be interested, there are maybe three teams that saw Rodgers on Wednesday's personnel notice and had to at least give thought to adding him the final six weeks of the season and perhaps into the playoffs. Maybe. A quick survey of NFL executives Wednesday leads us to those teams: JALEN HURTS TO REPORTEDLY MISS REMAINDER OF NFL SEASON AFTER BLOOD CLOTS FOUND IN QUARTERBACK'S LUNGS This is where we admit all of this is speculative because no source on the Patriots, Eagles, or Ravens is saying anything about Rodgers on Wednesday. But do these teams make sense on some level? Yes. The Eagles – They are 3-7 and in last place in the NFC East after losing multiple starters to trades, retirement, and injuries, with starting quarterback Jalen Hurts leading that cast with his season-ending blood clots situation. The Eagles have started Tanner McKee and lately have turned the offense over to Joe Milton. But it's a mess. They might decide its a salvageable mess with Rodgers because the division-leading Giants have games scheduled against the 49ers, Lions, Seahawks, and yes, the Eagles in the season-finale. A record under .500 might still win that division. The Ravens – This is admittedly a long shot. They're hoping they can get Lamar Jackson back from his broken and dislocated right thumb very late in the season and in the meantime they're hoping Jacoby Brissett can keep them in the playoff hunt. The problem is Brissett is 0-2 as the starter. So would the Ravens believe Rodgers is better? Definitely. But would Rodgers consider trying to rescue a team for a few weeks merely to turn it over to Jackson? Hard to imagine. The New England Patriots – Like the other two, they lost their starting quarterback to an injury. Drake Maybe has a ankle or leg fracture, depending on what report one believes, and his return is highly doubtful before the end of the regular season. But the Patriots have remained in the playoff hunt and their 5-5 record is just one game behind the Steelers. So might they see Rodgers as a boost? And might Rodgers see them as a chance to rally a team that last season went to the Super Bowl? OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Again, improbable. But not impossible. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Where does Aaron Rodgers’ interview with Pat McAfee rank among the wildest in sports history?
articles.summary: Watching Aaron Rodgers bury his own coach on Pat McAfee’s show got us thinking about the wildest interviews in sports, from Richard Sherman to Mike Tyson to Jim Everett.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers went on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday and said he found out from his tight end, Pat Freiermuth, that the Steelers were benching him. It seemed like a pretty newsworthy nugget that would lead sports talk shows for the next few days. It wasn't even close to the most interesting thing Rodgers said in the interview. Probably not even in the top five. Rodgers accused head coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep and snoring in meetings, alleged that McCarthy led a "1-2-3 PACKERS!" cheer at halftime of Sunday's loss to the Eagles, said he’d told his head coach to give up play-calling or release him, and claimed that he joked with GM Omar Khan about McCarthy's sleeping habits. Basically, if Rodgers was going down, he was taking McCarthy with him. The interview went so far off the rails that, within an hour, reports surfaced that Pittsburgh was waiving Rodgers. The Steelers made it official later Wednesday afternoon. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Pittsburgh had planned to keep him on the roster before he went on the air (which made sense to me, if only to keep him away from an AFC rival). STEELERS OFFICIALLY RELEASE AARON RODGERS AND KEEP COACH MIKE MCCARTHY ON THE JOB DESPITE EMBARRASSING CLAIMS I honestly couldn't believe what I was watching. I’ve seen guys hurt their chances of getting another job on the way out the door, but I’ve never seen a future Hall of Fame quarterback go on national TV to bury a head coach he personally vouched for and drag his own GM into it for good measure. Imagine being the next NFL coach who has to decide whether he wants Aaron Rodgers in his building. The closest comparison I can come up with is soccer legend Cristiano Ronaldo telling Piers Morgan he felt betrayed by Manchester United while he still played for Manchester United. The club and Ronaldo parted ways shortly thereafter. But that’s European soccer, so it doesn’t count. Let's talk about real sports and figure out which interviews belong in the conversation with Rodgers. First, a ground rule: news conferences are out. Once you open that door, the Bears are who Denny Green thought they were, Allen Iverson is talking about practice, Jim Mora wants to know why the hell you’re asking him about the PLAYOFFS?! And Mike Gundy is a man. He’s 40. Actually, Mike Gundy turns 60 next summer. How the hell was that almost 20 years ago? Let's start with a couple postgame interviews, which deserve an asterisk I’m willing to grade postgame interviews on a curve because the adrenaline is pumping. One that jumps to mind is former Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman talking to Erin Andrews after the NFC Championship Game in January 2014. Sherman had just tipped a Colin Kaepernick pass intended for Michael Crabtree into the hands of Malcolm Smith to send the Seahawks to the Super Bowl. Give me that play and a microphone, in that order, and I make no promises about what comes out of my mouth, either. Andrews asked Sherman the standard question in that situation. "The final play. Take me through it." Within seconds, Sherman had declared himself the best corner in the game, called Crabtree a "sorry receiver" and warned, "Don’t you ever talk about me!" "Who was talking about you?" Andrews asked. "Crabtree!" Poor Malcolm Smith. He caught the ball that sent Seattle to the Super Bowl, and thanks to Sherman, we only remember who didn’t catch it. "Crabtree!" Mike Tyson had 38 seconds of work under his belt when Jim Gray caught up with him in Glasgow in 2000. Gray wanted to know if that was the shortest fight of his career, which was a reasonable thing to ask a guy who’d just knocked out Lou Savarese in the amount of time it takes to melt half a stick of butter in a microwave. Tyson wasn’t interested in looking back at what had just happened. He had a message for Lennox Lewis. "I want to eat his children." There's no good way to segue from Mike Tyson into anything else, but I'm a pro, so I'm going to try. We go from eating children to an offer to (maybe) make some babies. (See? Total pro.) Legendary NFL quarterback Joe Namath found himself with a microphone in his face on the sidelines during a 2003 Jets game, a quarter-century after he retired. On the other end of that microphone was ESPN NFL reporter Suzy Kolber. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE To start, Namath gave a perfectly normal answer about Chad Pennington. Then Kolber asked what it meant to him to see the Jets struggling. "I want to kiss you," Namath told her before adding, "I couldn't care less about the team struggling." The Pro Football Hall of Famer actually got back to football long enough to point out that the Jets had struggled while Pennington was out. Then, in the very same answer, he circled back to what was really on his mind. "I want to kiss you." To her credit, Kolber handled it with class and professionalism and simply responded, "Thanks, Joe. I'll take that as a huge compliment." Namath later apologized to Kolber and admitted that he had been drinking for hours prior to the interview. These guys had time to think about it This is why Rodgers moves up the board for me. He chose to go on McAfee's show after finding out about his benching. Presumably, he had some time to think about what he might say. Bill Belichick had that same advantage when he sat down with CBS last year. He also had Jordon Hudson just outside the frame, which came in handy in case somebody tried to slip a tough question past him, like how the then-73-year-old football coach met his 24-year-old girlfriend. We’re not counting that one, though, because the best answer of the entire interview came from Hudson, even though the interview subject was Belichick. Bob Knight, on the other hand, was perfectly capable of making an interview uncomfortable all by himself. After Indiana fired him in 2000, Knight sat down with ESPN’s Jeremy Schaap to tell his side on live television. Schaap tried to get a question in, the two started arguing about who kept interrupting whom, and Knight offered a little career advice to the son of legendary sportswriter Dick Schaap. "You got a long way to go to be as good as your dad," Knight told him. "You better keep that in mind." Years later, Schaap said ESPN producer Willie Weinbaum had warned him before the interview that Knight would bring up his dad to try to throw him off. I used to produce Jeremy's ESPN Radio show, "The Sporting Life." If I’d been in Willie’s chair that day, I know exactly what I’d have said in Jeremy’s ear. "Told ya so." Remember Jim Gray from like 10 paragraphs ago? Ten years after Tyson, Gray was sitting across from LeBron James at a Boys & Girls Club in Greenwich, Connecticut. Millions of people wanted the answer to exactly one question. Before they got it, Gray asked LeBron if he was still biting his nails. There was plenty of time for non-basketball questions since ESPN had set aside an hour for "The Decision." LeBron eventually let Cleveland know he was taking his talents to South Beach. The special raised more than $2 million for the Boys & Girls Clubs, so I’ll give him credit for that. The interview itself wasn’t especially crazy. What’s crazy is that a guy wrote into Bill Simmons’ mailbag suggesting LeBron announce his decision on TV, and seven months later, millions of people were waiting for Jim Gray to get past the fingernails. Then there’s Dennis Rodman, who went to North Korea in 2014 with a group of former NBA players to play an exhibition game for Kim Jong Un’s birthday. Take a second and read that sentence again. We haven’t even gotten to the interview. CNN's Chris Cuomo asked whether Rodman would speak up for Kenneth Bae, an American being held in North Korea. Rodman started demanding to know whether Cuomo understood what Bae had done. Sitting alongside him was former Knicks forward Charles Smith, left to explain that the guys were there to play basketball. Rodman later apologized to Bae’s family. Of all the people in this story, Smith might be the one I’d most like to interview. What did Dennis tell him the itinerary was? Two heavyweights, two guys named Jim* and a quick word from Ichiro Honorable mention for the funniest answer to an innocent question goes to Ichiro Suzuki. Bob Costas asked for his favorite American expression. Ichiro answered in English, describing August in Kansas City as "hotter than two rats in a f---ing wool sock." Good luck asking a follow-up. Costas was laughing too hard to get one out anyway. In 1974, ABC sat Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier down with Howard Cosell to watch their first fight ahead of their rematch. Maybe it was a simpler time, but I like to think somebody at ABC genuinely wanted to hear two guys who were about to beat the hell out of each other talk about the last time they beat the hell out of each other. The full episode of Wide World of Sports is below. If you’re here for the fight that took place in the studio, skip to about the 56-minute mark. The amazing part to me is that the replay had made it to the 10th round before Ali and Frazier went after each other. Try that in 2026. If those guys are still sitting in their chairs by the end of the first round, some promoter is pulling one of them aside to remind him they’ve still got tickets to sell. Do yourself a favor and watch Cosell when they end up wrestling on the studio floor. The man stays in his chair and calls the action. I can’t say I blame him. What’s he supposed to do, get between Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier? At least those two left the interviewer out of it. Which brings us to Jim Rome. I never had any intention of figuring out who finished fourth or seventh on this list. I do know who finished first. In 1994, Jim Everett agreed to go on ESPN2 with Jim Rome, who’d taken to calling the quarterback "Chris," after female tennis great Chris Evert, to suggest he was afraid of getting hit. My favorite part is when Everett starts warning Rome about calling him Chris to his face one more time, and Rome cuts in to make sure he gets credit for the first two. "I already did it twice!" Both men understand the terms. There’s still time to ask about football. "Chris." Everett got up and knocked Rome out of his chair. A producer stepped in, and ESPN2 cut away. For those of you keeping score at home, Jim Rome did technically win that bet. So where does Rodgers land? Pretty high, in my book. Sherman barely had time to take his helmet off. Third-year wide receiver Roman Wilson returned this week from injury, Michael Pittman Jr. returned to practice and rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard has been solid for them this season. articles.title: Dak Prescott's 1,000-yard, 11-touchdown surge over three games makes Cowboys heavy Thanksgiving favorites
articles.summary: Happy Thanksgiving! Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys already beat the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 this season ahead of their Thanksgiving rematch.
articles.body: Happy Thanksgiving to all you turkeys out there. I hope your plate is full, your turkey is moist, the stuffing is aplenty, and most of all, that we make a ton of money today. By the time this game comes on, you probably will be either about to start your dinner or heading to the in-laws for the next meal. What could be better today? Well, a win in this game would be a bit of help, and let’s see if we can get that with the Eagles and Cowboys. The Philadelphia Eagles were impressive on Sunday, and that’s saying something. The team has been a bit of a disaster this season, specifically with Jalen Hurts and his injury situation. They come into today’s game with a 3-7 record and are probably just trying to play spoiler for any opponent at this point in their season. They aren’t mathematically eliminated from the postseason or anything, but they might as well be. And that’s taking into consideration the win they had Sunday. Before we go and say that Joe Milton III is the answer at quarterback, let’s just admit that the Steelers aren’t exactly a great team. They are fine, but a really bad first quarter did Pittsburgh in for the game. The Eagles only scored six points the remainder of the game, and the Steelers outscored them 16-6 from the start of the second quarter on. A win is a win, but I don’t think want anyone thinking the Eagles have figured something out. The good news for them is that they at least put up some points against a defense that is certainly better than what Dallas has to offer. EAGLES QB JOE MILTON SHARES THAT HE SAYS HIS DAUGHTER'S NAME TO CALM NERVES BEFORE THROWING A DEEP BALL The Dallas Cowboys are basically just running back what they did last season. I hate to bash the team because I was pretty high on them before the season started, but their only method of victory is to have Dak Prescott go bonkers and throw for a million yards and 10 touchdowns a game. Obviously, I’m exaggerating here, but he does have almost exactly 1,000 passing yards and 11 touchdowns over the past three games. If he had any semblance of a defense this season, he might be in the MVP conversation as I predicted before the year. BUT… he doesn’t. His defense is awful. They are ranked near the bottom in passing and rushing yards allowed, and they are giving up a ton of points. It means Prescott has to be near perfect for them to win. Even when he was close against the 49ers, they still lost by six because the defense couldn’t give him any help. Dallas is a fun team to watch, but it has to be frustrating for true fans of the club. COWBOYS STAR QUINNEN WILLIAMS REPEATS SIX WORD ANSWER 12 TIMES IN PRESSER AFTER MAJOR COACHING CHANGE Prescott and the Cowboys have already beaten the Eagles once this season. They went into Philadelphia and won 38-21. I’m not really sure why they aren’t bigger favorites in this one, outside of maybe because Philly looked a bit better with Milton under center. I like the Cowboys to cover the -8.5 in this game, and I think their team total is a good look as well. Prescott has been playing great lately and has already shown he can rack up points against the Eagles' defense. A win from Philly last week also makes me think they will stumble this week. Sometimes a bad team just wants to get a win and then rests a bit the next week. Give me the Cowboys -8.5 and give me their team total over. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s Chiefs future remains a mystery after 100 Arrowhead games, with one answer keeping fans guessing
articles.summary: Travis Kelce gave Kansas City Chiefs fans another reason to celebrate after reaching 100 regular-season appearances at Arrowhead Stadium.
articles.body: Travis Kelce gave Kansas City Chiefs fans another reason to celebrate after reaching 100 regular-season appearances at Arrowhead Stadium. His performance against the Arizona Cardinals included two touchdowns, but the bigger talking point came later on his podcast. Jason Kelce tried to turn his younger brother’s celebration into a retirement update, asking whether he planned to return for another season. Travis refused to give him a clear answer. At a time when his future is drawing attention, the Chiefs tight end made it clear that he has not made any announcement about 2027.Travis Kelce avoids confirming another season with the ChiefsThe retirement conversation came during the latest episode of New Heights. Jason brought up Travis' postgame comment about playing another 100 games, sensing an opportunity to get some clarity about his brother's plans.Travis was quick to admit that reaching another 100 appearances might be unrealistic. However, he did not rule out extending his career.“Yeah, you’re right. I won’t. But cheers to 100 more. Who knows how many I’ll get to,” Travis said.Jason followed up with a direct question, asking whether his brother was confirming that he would play another season. The response offered little relief to Chiefs supporters hoping for an early decision.“No, I’m not confirming it,” Travis replied. “I’m not confirming.”It was a playful exchange, but the distinction was important. Kelce did not announce his retirement, nor did he commit to returning in 2027. For now, his plans remain open.Jason's curiosity was understandable after what his brother had just accomplished. Against Arizona, Kelce caught six passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City's 34-7 victory. It was hardly the performance of a player struggling to remain involved in the offense.The Chiefs also have an important Thanksgiving matchup against the Buffalo Bills ahead. Kelce's immediate attention is on helping Kansas City maintain its form rather than settling questions about the next stage of his career.Travis Kelce's Arrowhead record adds to his growing legacyThe Arizona game carried significance beyond the two touchdowns. Kelce became only the fourth player in Chiefs history to appear in 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead, joining Dustin Colquitt, Will Shields and Nick Lowery.For the tight end, the achievement had a personal meaning that went beyond another entry in the record books.“It’s been home for me for 14 years,” Travis said.He also recalled the concerts and other events he had experienced at the stadium, explaining how much the venue had become part of his life.“I’ve had so much history and so many things that mean so much to me happen at Arrowhead,” he said.His latest performance also moved him past Rob Gronkowski into third place for career touchdowns by a tight end, including postseason games. Kelce now has 110, behind Tony Gonzalez's 115 and Antonio Gates' 118.His numbers this season explain why another campaign remains a reasonable topic. Through 10 games, he had 41 receptions for 586 yards and four touchdowns. His 87.8 grade also placed him third in PFN's TE Impact rankings following the Arizona victory.Kelce also gave credit to his quarterback when discussing Kansas City's recent success.“Pat Mahomes is playing his tail off right now,” he said.That connection remains central to the Chiefs' offense. Kelce has spent 14 seasons building his place in Kansas City, and his latest milestone showed that he can still produce at a high level. Jason tried to turn the occasion into a retirement announcement. His brother was having none of it. Another season is possible, but Kelce is not ready to put a date on his final appearance at Arrowhead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Chad Johnson laid out his dream scenario when hoping that Aaron Rodgers comes back. Rodgers was released by the Steelers around an hour after the critical co...
articles.body:
Chad Johnson laid out his dream scenario when hoping that Aaron Rodgers comes back.

Rodgers was released by the Steelers around an hour after the critical comments he made about coach Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show.

While the quarterback said it himself during the interview that the chances of him returning to the team were likely ruled out, Johnson pitched what his "perfect world" outcome would be.

Chad Johnson wants both Aaron Rodgers and Antonio Brown to come back following Steelers exit

On Nightcap, Chad Johnson said that he hopes to see Aaron Rodgers come back despite knowing that this is "not possible".

'Ochocinco' then went one step further than this by revealing another highly unlikely scenario that he'd like to see come to fruition.

"Hey, in a perfect world for me, I know it's not possible, but Aaron Rodgers comes back. And guess who comes out of retirement?"

Johnson then added, "84", which his co-hosts successfully identified as former Super Bowl champion Antonio Brown.

"Yeah," he said. "Hey, come on, baby. AB, come on back. Come on."

Brown, who played for the Steelers from 2010-2018, hasn't played an NFL game since he walked off the field mid-game during his time with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2022.

It was pointed out to Johnson that this "ship sailed long ago", but as he stated at the start of his comments, this is simply his dream scenario.

"Let me tell you something," he added. "One thing about sales: you can always hit a U-turn. Hey, AB, come out right now."

The Los Angeles Rams ran all over the Green Bay Packers en route to a 26-13 win on Thanksgiving Eve. Running back Blake Corum starred with a career-high 184 yards and a touchdown as the Rams finished with 241 rushing yards.

Corum recalled what Rams head coach Sean McVay told the team, which was that the "most physical team" would come out on top. Corum believes their performance spoke for itself .

"And I think we were that," Corum said, per ESPN's Sarah Barshop. "I know we were that."

With the win, the Rams extended their impressive winning streak to five games in a row as they improved to 7-4 on the season. Corum has been instrumental in the Rams' resurgence. He has scored a rushing touchdown in each of those five wins , while picking up 508 rushing yards.

The Rams were once again without star wide receiver Puka Nacua, who has been ruled out for the season due to MCL surgery . With the Rams missing their top two receivers, they have rushed for over 200 yards in each of their last two games.

articles.title: Predicting winners for all 3 NFL Thanksgiving Day games
articles.summary: Picking the winner and the score of all 3 games on Thanksgiving day, 2026.
articles.body:
Thanksgiving's NFL schedule features three important matchups with plenty of playoff implications as the regular season enters its final stretch. The Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions open the day with an NFC North showdown, followed by an NFC East rivalry between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys. Kansas City and Buffalo close the holiday slate with another major AFC matchup. Each game presents a different challenge, but all three have the potential to deliver plenty of points.

Chicago and Detroit enter Thanksgiving with matching 8-2 records, but the Bears have several reasons to believe they can leave Ford Field with a victory. Chicago has won five straight games, while Detroit has won six in a row. This is a matchup between two of the NFC's best teams, and the Bears' ability to control possession could be a major factor.

Chicago averages 26.2 points and 376 yards per game. The Bears also lead the NFL in time of possession, averaging 34:06 per contest. That ability to sustain drives could help keep Jared Goff and Detroit's offense on the sideline. Caleb Williams has thrown for 1,727 yards and 10 touchdowns, while D'Andre Swift has contributed 627 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns.

Detroit's offense is capable of putting up points in a hurry. The Lions average 28.8 points per game, and Goff has already thrown 20 touchdown passes against just four interceptions. Jahmyr Gibbs has been one of the NFL's most productive players, leading the league with 1,502 scrimmage yards and 15 scrimmage touchdowns. Amon-Ra St. Brown also has 70 receptions for 792 yards and eight touchdowns.

The Bears have the offensive balance to keep pace, and Williams has thrown multiple touchdown passes in each of his four career starts against Detroit. Chicago's ability to control the clock and finish drives could make the difference in a high-scoring divisional matchup.

Dallas enters this Thanksgiving matchup with momentum after putting 51 points on the board against Tennessee last week. The Cowboys are 5-6, while Philadelphia has struggled to a 3-7 record. The Eagles earned a 19-16 win over Pittsburgh in Week 11, but their offense may struggle to keep pace with the Cowboys' high-powered attack, even with Dallas's defensive struggles.

The Cowboys defeated the Eagles 38-21 in their Week 7 meeting. Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes in that game, while running back Javonte Williams rushed for 155 yards and a touchdown. Prescott is coming off another impressive performance, becoming one of just five quarterbacks in NFL history to record multiple career games with at least 300 passing yards, four touchdown passes, and a rushing touchdown.

CeeDee Lamb gives Prescott another major advantage in the passing game. Lamb leads the NFL with 88 receptions and ranks second with 1,108 receiving yards. His ability to create consistent production should put pressure on an Eagles defense that needs to find a way to slow down Dallas' passing attack.

Philadelphia's quarterback situation is another important storyline. Joe Milton is expected to lead the offense, and the Eagles have averaged just 16.7 points per game this season. Dallas has defensive vulnerabilities, but its recent offensive production makes it difficult to pick against the Cowboys at home. Expect Prescott and Lamb to lead another productive afternoon.

The Thanksgiving night matchup could be the most entertaining game of the day. Kansas City enters at 8-2, while Buffalo owns a 9-1 record. Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen are meeting for the 11th time, adding another chapter to one of the NFL's biggest quarterback rivalries.

Buffalo has had the better regular-season results against Kansas City in recent years, winning five of the six meetings since 2020. However, the Chiefs have won all four postseason matchups during that stretch. Mahomes also has a strong track record in Thursday games, recording 19 touchdown passes and a 106.5 passer rating in nine career Thursday starts.

Allen has consistently produced against Kansas City. In 10 career starts against the Chiefs, including the postseason, he has averaged 307.9 total yards per game and accounted for 27 touchdowns. He is coming off a 304-yard passing performance against Miami, while Mahomes threw for 324 yards and helped Kansas City defeat Arizona 34-7.

Buffalo has the advantage in the standings, but Kansas City's recent offensive performance and Mahomes' experience in high-pressure matchups make the Chiefs an appealing pick. Allen should keep the Bills competitive, but Mahomes finds a way to deliver another important victory for Kansas City.

articles.body:
Skip Bayless has taken a brutal shot at Micah Parsons following the defensive star's impressive return from an 11-month injury absence. The Green Bay Packers pass rusher recorded a sack in his comeback game against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night.

Parsons made his first appearance since suffering a torn ACL and meniscus damage against the Denver Broncos last December. Despite playing just 26 of Green Bay's 71 defensive snaps, he finished with one sack, two quarterback hits and four pressures in a 26-13 defeat.

However, Bayless was more interested in reminding Parsons of his record with the Dallas Cowboys . The die-hard Cowboys fan has always been outspoken about the franchise's fortunes and was clearly not prepared to let Parsons forget his postseason performances.

"I just saw Micah Parsons do something he did only once in 4 Cowboys playoff games, 3 of 'em losses – he had a sack!" Bayless posted.

Parsons was an outstanding regular-season performer during his Cowboys career, establishing himself as one of the NFL's most feared defensive players. However, his playoff impact never quite matched those standards.

The 27-year-old's return against the Rams was encouraging, particularly given the severity of his injury and limited playing time. However, Bayless used the occasion to take another dig at a player who once represented Dallas' hopes of ending their long wait for playoff success.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Accused Mike McCarthy of Falling Asleep in Meetings. Hours Later, the Steelers Cut Him
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers released Aaron Rodgers on November 25 after he publicly accused coach Mike McCarthy of sleeping during meetings and missing team acti...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers released Aaron Rodgers on November 25 after he publicly accused coach Mike McCarthy of sleeping during meetings and missing team activities.

The decision ended the 42-year-old quarterback's second season with the franchise. The four-time NFL MVP had returned in May on a one-year contract that included $22 million guaranteed.

Rodgers and McCarthy worked together in Green Bay from 2006 through 2018 and won Super Bowl XLV. Rodgers had supported the coach's hiring in Pittsburgh after Mike Tomlin's departure earlier this year.

Rodgers has previously said 2026 would be his final NFL season. His exit leaves open whether he will finish that year with another team or has already played his last game.

Rodgers Explains His Break With the Steelers

At 11:10 p.m. on November 24, team spokesman Burt Lauten announced that Mason Rudolph would start against the Denver Broncos on Friday, November 27, and Rodgers would be inactive. The announcement followed McCarthy's public backing of Rodgers on Monday and the quarterback's work with the first team Tuesday.

Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show , Rodgers said he learned about the change during a telephone conversation with tight end Pat Freiermuth. He said McCarthy had not told him directly that he was being benched.

Rodgers was excused from Wednesday's team activities and said during the interview that he would not return to Pittsburgh. He also described asking McCarthy to change the offensive play-calling arrangement, saying the team should release him if it would not make changes or intended to bench him.

Rodgers Describes Snoring and a Halftime Mistake

The quarterback recalled a November 18 meeting in which, he said, McCarthy arrived late and began snoring within about 10 minutes. Rodgers said the coach woke himself, shuffled papers, fell asleep again and eventually left the room.

Rodgers described his concerns as recurring, saying he had raised them privately and that McCarthy had denied falling asleep. He argued that missed meetings and inadequate preparation affected assistants and players whose livelihoods depended on the team's performance.

He also recalled McCarthy ending a huddle during halftime of the November 22 loss to Philadelphia by saying, "1-2-3 Packers." ESPN reported that multiple league sources corroborated Rodgers' account, including the meeting and locker-room incidents.

McCarthy Responds to Rodgers and Defends His Decision

Addressing reporters later Wednesday, McCarthy said the benching was his decision. He described Rodgers' demand as an ultimatum that was "clearly out of his job description," according to Sports Illustrated .

McCarthy acknowledged the huddle slip as an "embarrassing moment." On the dispute over how Rodgers learned the news, he said there had been continuing efforts to reach the quarterback and communication with his representatives, although he did not know the details of every conversation.

The coach also expressed confidence that he retained the players' support after meeting with the team's leadership council. He described those discussions as direct and honest and said he appreciated the urgency the players showed afterward.

Rodgers Enters Waivers With Pittsburgh Still in Contention

NFL Network reported that Pittsburgh initially intended to keep Rodgers after benching him but changed course following the interview. Because his release came after the trade deadline, other teams can claim him through waivers. If he goes unclaimed, he becomes an unrestricted free agent.

The Steelers entered the week at 6-4 after consecutive losses to Cincinnati and Philadelphia. Rodgers completed 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions across 10 starts this season.

articles.title: Cowboys vs Eagles national anthem singer: What to know about Lauren Daigle
articles.summary: Two-time Grammy winner Lauren Daigle takes center stage before the Cowboys and Eagles kick off their Thanksgiving Day matchup.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles will meet on Thanksgiving Day at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, for an important NFC East battle.

The Cowboys (5-6) are coming off a dominant win over the Tennessee Titans , while the Eagles (3-7) will be looking to build on last week's 19-16 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Since it's the middle game of the NFL's three-course Thanksgiving menu (4:30 p.m. ET, Fox), viewers shouldn't have to miss any of the pregame pageantry. Just before kickoff, two-time Grammy Award-winning singer Lauren Daigle will perform her rendition of "The Star-Spangled Banner."

From 'Butt Fumbles' to Barry Sanders: NFL’s Most unforgettable Thanksgiving moments

Who is singing the national anthem at Eagles-Cowboys Thanksgiving game?

Contemporary Christian singer Lauren Daigle will be the featured performer and sing "The Star-Spangled Banner" before the Cowboys and Eagles kick off at AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving Day.

Daigle first reached No. 1 on the Billboard Top Christian Albums chart in 2015 with her debut "How Can It Be." She achieved crossover success with the single "You Say," which peaked at No. 29 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in 2018. That song, and the album "Look Up Child" earned her a pair of Grammy Awards in 2019 for Best Contemporary Christian Music Album and Best Contemporary Christian Music Performance/Song.

Daigle is no stranger to performing in front of NFL fans.

She sang "America the Beautiful" alongside Trombone Shorty before Super Bowl 59 in her home state of Louisiana.

In addition to her two Grammy wins, she was also nominated in 2016, 2017 and 2024. She has won four American Music Awards as well.

articles.title: Broncos WR Courtland Sutton shares his 'highlights' after zero-catch game

articles.body:
Denver Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton is truly a team-first player.

The veteran receiver has repeatedly said his biggest priority is winning, not stacking up individual stats. That was apparent on Sunday when Sutton was held without a catch and there wasn't even a hint of complaints from Sutton as the Broncos secured a 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders .

"It's unusual, but sometimes that can happen," coach Sean Payton said of Sutton being held without a catch. "I think it's the things that you love about his makeup and his leadership. He's done this long enough. I know for him, the unselfish part of just wanting to win. Now there's plays, it's hard to explain. There are plays that are like his play and sometimes it happened last week with Evan [Engram] on a few plays where I don't know that I would've said that first third-and-long he's getting... So it's sometimes the nature of what you get coverage-wise. As great of a player as he is, the consistency of leadership and work ethic is something that I really appreciate."

Sutton took to Instagram earlier this week to show his "highlights" from the most recent win (pictures of him blocking for teammates):

Sutton has displayed a team-first mentality, and that hasn't gone unnoticed by Payton. As a reward, it wouldn't be surprising to see the Broncos scheme up some plays specifically for Sutton against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday.

The Los Angeles Rams extended their winning streak to five games after outclassing the Green Bay Packers , 26-13, at SoFi Stadium in the NFL's first-ever game on Thanksgiving Eve.

The Rams improved to 7-4 and spoiled the return of Micah Parsons from a knee injury he sustained in December.

The Rams were relentless on the ground, leaving the Packers in shambles. Los Angeles had 47 carries for 241 yards, led by Blake Corum, who had a league-high 32 carries for a career-high 184 yards and a touchdown.

On defense, Myles Garrett had three tackles and two quarterback hits.

After the game, Garrett and Parsons shared a moment on the field. Garrett played in his third straight game since recovering from a knee injury he suffered in Week 1.

It was cool to see two of the league's top defenders show respect to each other.

Parsons logged one tackle, one sack, and two quarterback hits after an 11-month absence.

Garrett tipped his hat to Parsons, as reported by NBC Los Angeles' Nick Hamilton.

"He's just coming back. He had a good game on limited reps. Just proud of him, happy that he's back out there on the field. He can start to feel like himself," said the two-time Defensive Player of the Year.

"Seeing him doing it, being back to who he is, with a smile on his face, and being dominant, I think that's all what we want to see."

Parsons, however, was disappointed with the loss , acknowledging the tough reality as the Packers try to stay in the hunt for the playoffs.

articles.title: 49ers Get Potential Injury Boost Ahead of Seahawks Game
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers took a step to add depth up front. The team opened the practice window for offensive lineman Austen Pleasants on Wednesday, per Kyle...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers took a step to add depth up front. The team opened the practice window for offensive lineman Austen Pleasants on Wednesday, per Kyle Madson of Niners Wire. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said he could be ready as early as Week 12.

The timing is no accident. Right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a season-ending ankle injury in the 49ers' Week 11 win over the Minnesota Vikings. Vederian Lowe took over for him, but there are not many options behind Lowe.

Pleasants would give them another one. He is still working his way back from a knee injury and must be fully cleared before he can return to the active roster.

Shanahan did not rule it out. "Yeah, he is a possibility," he said on Wednesday.

He explained that Pleasants has been healthy for a while. "He's been healthy for a few weeks now. With losing Colton, it makes sense to get him out practicing and we'll see how this week goes," Shanahan said. "If he's ready to go and if he is we'll make a decision."

Pleasants got hurt in the 49ers' second preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers . He spent a lot of that game at left tackle while the team looked for its best option at that spot.

Tackle is his natural position, and it is where he has played most of his time in San Francisco. He has appeared in eight games over the last two seasons, including a start at left tackle in Week 18.

Why Pleasants Matters to the San Francisco 49ers

The 49ers' offense has been rolling, and the line has been a big part of it. McKivitz played every offensive snap this season before the injury, so replacing him is not a small task.

An extra tackle gives Shanahan more ways to handle injuries, and he has already seen how quickly they can happen.

San Francisco hosts the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday at 1:25 p.m. PT at Levi's Stadium. Pleasants could be an option for that game if the 49ers decide he is ready.

The practice window gives them time to look. Shanahan said they will see how the week goes and then make a decision.

articles.title: Ex-Packer James Jones Makes Feelings Clear About Aaron Rodgers’ Controversial Shots at Mike McCarthy: ‘This Could End Him’
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers is taking heat from inside his old locker room. James Jones, a former NFL player who played with Rodgers in Green Bay, tore into the quarterbac...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers is taking heat from inside his old locker room. James Jones, a former NFL player who played with Rodgers in Green Bay, tore into the quarterback early Thursday over Rodgers' recent comments about his former head coach, Mike McCarthy.

Jones was reacting to Rodgers' claim that McCarthy slept in meetings. Rodgers made the comments on The Pat McAfee Show earlier in the day before officially being released by the Steelers. Jones did not hold back, and he said he is far from the only former teammate who feels that way.

The blowup comes during a rough stretch for Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. Pittsburgh lost 19-16 at Philadelphia on Sunday, and Pro Football Network QB Impact grades place Rodgers near the bottom of the league's quarterbacks this season.

James Jones Makes Feelings Clear About Aaron Rodgers

Jones went live on Speakeasy just after midnight Thursday and made clear where his old Packers teammates stand. "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates on there right now. And ain't none of 'em on twelve side," Jones said.

Jones pointed to the long history between the two men. He noted that Rodgers and McCarthy have been together for nearly 15 years, which he called more than half of Rodgers' career. That history, in Jones' view, is what made the public criticism sting so much.

Jones said the episode did not match anything he saw in Green Bay. "I don't never remember none of this at the Packers," he said. He also brushed off the idea that dozing in a meeting says much about anyone. "I also think this is weak because players sleep in meetings. I slept in a couple of meetings," Jones said.

For Jones, the problem was not whether Rodgers was telling the truth. It was where he said it. "Whether it's right, whether it's wrong, I don't care about none of that," Jones said. He argued that a quarterback and his coach "meet every single day," so any concerns about the locker room could have been raised face to face instead of on a national show.

Jones was careful to say his anger did not come from a bad relationship with Rodgers. "Aaron know how much the game meant to me," he said, and he made a point of saying he loves Rodgers. He said he would call out any former teammate who did the same thing, and he called it "weak."

His biggest worry was the damage to McCarthy. Jones said Rodgers is near the end, with more than 20 years in the league and a likely trip to the Hall of Fame waiting for him. McCarthy, he said, is in a very different spot. "Coach Mike is still trying to coach. This could end him," Jones said.

Plenty of fans shared Jones' anger, and some saw a bigger pattern. One fan argued that Rodgers has "a pervasive pattern of behavior towards NFL coaches" and has clashed with a coach on each team he has played for, calling it part of his personality.

"In case you haven't noticed Aaron Rodgers has a pervasive pattern of behavior towards NFL coaches. Each team Aaron Rodgers has been on he has a problem with the coach. The last time he went after Robert Saleh. It's his personality. Dark traits," they tweeted.

Others were even harsher. One fan wrote that Rodgers is "a complete fraud as a teammate and respected player."

Not everyone put all the blame on Rodgers, though. One fan took aim at McCarthy, claiming the coach never told Rodgers directly that he was benched. That same fan still pointed to the silence around Rodgers in Pittsburgh: "Not a single Steelers player spoke up in defense. Tells you a lot, man."

Another fan landed right where Jones did, saying the issue is airing private matters at all. "Keep your dirty laundry in-house. It makes you small when you air this stuff in public," the fan wrote, adding that "a locker room is a holy place."

The fight is playing out while the Steelers' offense sputters. In Week 11 at Philadelphia, Pittsburgh lost 19-16 even though it outgained the Eagles 255 total yards to 214 and did not turn the ball over. The Eagles had one turnover. Rodgers went 30 of 44 for 227 yards and one touchdown, but the Steelers could not turn the yardage advantage into a win.

CHECK THE DEPTH CHARTS: PFN's NFL Depth Charts

PFN's own grades back up the struggles. Rodgers earned a 69 Impact grade against the Eagles, which ranked 23rd of 26 graded quarterbacks that week. Through Week 12, his season Impact grade sits at 67.1, 29th of 33 graded quarterbacks.

Those numbers leave Rodgers with little cushion as the criticism piles up. Jones made his point plainly: he still loves Rodgers, but he thinks going public with these claims about McCarthy was the wrong move. And by Jones' account, none of the old teammates in his group texts are on Rodgers' side.

articles.title: Here’s a 1,000-word analysis on whether or not the Patriots should sign Aaron Rodgers, and you can probably guess where this is going
articles.summary: Why the Patriots should, and shouldn’t, sign Aaron Rodgers after his release from the Steelers.
articles.body:
Last week, when the Indianapolis Colts released starting quarterback Daniel Jones, we took a deep dive into the why or the why not he should end up getting signed by the New England Patriots. Ultimately, our verdict was that Jones coming to Foxborough appeared unlikely to happen for a variety of reasons and, lo and behold, it looks like the team agreed with that assessment: it continues backing Tommy DeVito as the starting quarterback with Drake Maye sidelined for the foreseeable future with a fractured fibula.

However, a new challenger has now emerged — and it's a big one: Aaron Rodgers, a former Pro Football Hall of Famer and one of the best quarterbacks the NFL has ever seen.

Rodgers was unceremoniously cut by the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday after his relationship with the team and head coach Mike McCarthy in particular had soured, to put it mildly. With the expectation being that he will go through waivers unclaimed due to the nature of his contract, the 43-year-old could be on the open market by Thursday afternoon, ready to be picked up for a fraction of the cost.

The initial assessment of Rodgers as a Patriots candidate ranged from "no" to "hell no," but there have been some vocal advocates both among local media circles, former Patriots players, and our little community here. Could it therefore be that the initial reaction was too harsh?

Let's put on our analytical hazmat suits and find out.

Why the Patriots should sign Aaron Rodgers

He is no longer the elite passer he was in the 2010s and the early 2020s, but Rodgers has still played some serviceable football during his one and a half years in Pittsburgh. This season, for example, he has completed 60.9% of his pass attempts for 2,241 yards with 16 touchdowns and six interceptions.

That second number, and his career-long ball security as a whole, might be key from a Patriots perspective.

Rodgers' 1.7% interception rate this year is 11th-best in the NFL, and would be a clear improvement over Drake Maye's 4.0% and backup Tommy DeVito's 3.1% (even though the latter's number needs to be taken with a grain of salt given the limited sample size). No, he wouldn't challenge Maye's status as QB1; at this point in their careers and despite his recent ball security issues, the third-year passer's ceiling is significantly higher than Rodgers'. That said, he could be a suitable stop-gap and help settle down a unit whose biggest issue besides injuries has been turnovers.

The real question in that regard would be whether or not the Patriots would trust Rodgers more than DeVito to lead the offense for the next few weeks, and put the team in position for a playoff run. Historically, that wouldn't even be a question; we are talking about four-time league MVP Aaron Rodgers.

The gap between him and a backup has shrunk significantly from his peak. Nonetheless, one could still make the argument that even a player ranked 29th among qualifying quarterbacks with -0.022 expected points added per play would be the best available option for a team like New England. And if that player is one with the experience of 22 NFL seasons, the argument tilts even further in his favor.

Why the Patriots shouldn't sign Aaron Rodgers

Rodgers having lost a step is something the Patriots would have to live with; they probably wouldn't be too worried about that in a vacuum. The same is true about him having to learn a new system and building chemistry with an unfamiliar supporting cast. If they believed in him, they probably would find a way to adjust accordingly and make it work for the handful of weeks he would be needed to.

The anti-Rodgers argument, however, has little to do with his play or lack of in-system experience relative to Tommy DeVito. It is all about him and his impact on the culture Mike Vrabel has been trying to build since his arrival as head coach in January 2025.

Rodgers has been a divisive figure for a while now, but what happened before his release on Wednesday was unprecedented even by his or the NFL as a whole's standards. Appearing on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show less than 24 hours after being informed that he would be benched for backup quarterback Mason Rudolph, he aired his grievances pretty much unfiltered. A few hours later, and to nobody's surprise, he was cut.

Since then, additional details have come out, including Rodgers threatening to quit the team unless he was allowed to call Pittsburgh's offense himself. Other details revealed by him have been confirmed to be true, but him presenting them on national television is an unprecedented development.

The Patriots inviting that into their building, especially with a 5-5 record and some pressure already bubbling inside the team, would reek of desperation — desperation a team that played in the Super Bowl less than 10 months ago and has the pieces in place to remain competitive for years to come, shouldn't feel. Yes, Tommy DeVito might be a downgrade from him, but he would be no live grenade tossed into the locker room that could explode at any moment if things doesn't go its way.

Sure, there is a chance that won't happen again and that Rodgers lands somewhere between repentant and out to prove people wrong, but would taking this chance be worth it for a bottom-third starter?

The Patriots won't sign Aaron Rodgers as a free agent, nor should they. It's as simple as that, and as noted above is not about his diminished abilities as a quarterback or inexperience in a Josh McDaniels system.

It is, however, as simple as this: signing Rodgers after Wednesday's events would go against every message the supposed culture-building head coach Mike Vrabel has preached for the last year-plus. Every phrase about putting the team first or holding oneself accountable was tossed out the window by him, and while it might only have been a spur-of-the-moment event in the aftermath of significant in-team disagreements, adding him would still not be worth the gamble.

You can't build a culture in six weeks, but you sure can start tearing one down. And Rodgers, well, he is a sledgehammer.

What do you think about Aaron Rodgers? Should the Patriots pursue him, or steer clear of him? Please head down to the comment section to share your thoughts or visit this Feed post by Pats Pulpit community member BBREBOZO .

articles.title: Top-5 Thanksgiving Day plays in Miami Dolphins history
articles.summary: Ranking best Dolphins plays on Thanksgiving Day.
articles.body:
Thanksgiving Day means a few things to most Americans: food, family and football. And while the Miami Dolphins won't be playing on this year's Turkey Day, they've had some very memorable moments for the franchise on Thanksgiving in the past.

The Dolphins have played eight times on Thanksgiving — winning five of those contests. And in those games, they've had their fair share of incredible plays, including one of the most infamous blunders in the history of the National Football League.

So before Mom busts out the gravy and stuffing, before Dad cracks open his first cold one of the day, and before the kids break out the ol' pigskin in the backyard, let's rank the top-5 plays in Miami Dolphins' Thanksgiving Day game history.

5. Bob Griese throws 45-yard touchdown to Paul Warfield (Dolphins vs. Cowboys – 1973)

On November 22nd, 1973, the defending Super Bowl Champion Miami Dolphins faced a very good Dallas Cowboys team on Thanksgiving Day. Early on in the contest, future Hall-of-Fame quarterback Bob Griese hit future Hall-of-Fame wide receiver Paul Warfield for a 45-yard touchdown in a game that would eventually end in a 14-7 Dolphins victory.

4. Sammy Knight returns interception 70-yards (Dolphins vs. Cowboys – 2003)

On a day that saw the Dolphins' defense sack Cowboys' quarterback Quincy Carter five times and intercept three of his passes, Sammy Knight's pick and subsequent 70-yard return was one for the highlight reels. Knight joined Patrick Surtain and Zach Thomas as beneficiaries of errant Cowboy Carter throws that afternoon, and the Dolphins went back to South Florida with a 40-21 victory.

3. Jason Taylor returns fumble for 34-yard touchdown (Dolphins vs. Cowboys – 2003)

Sammy Knight wasn't the only Dolphins defender with a signature play during Miami's win over Dallas in 2003. Hall-of-Fame defensive end Jason Taylor also thrilled fans of the aqua and orange that Thanksgiving with a 34-yard scoop and score after a Quincy Carter fumble. Dressed in throwback uniforms that day, the Dolphins defense dominated Dallas en route to a big Turkey Day victory.

2. Keith Byars runs for 77-yard touchdown in the snow (Dolphins vs. Cowboys – 1993)

One of the most memorable plays in NFL history would come later in this contest, however, without Keith Byars' 77-yard touchdown scamper through the Texas snow earlier in the game, we may have never seen it. After Byars crossed the goalline in Dallas, he would celebrate by making a snow angel on the Texas Stadium turf in Irving.

1. Leon Lett fumbles, Dellenbach recovers, Dolphins win (Dolphins vs. Cowboys – 1993)

The most famous play in Thanksgiving Day history came in the Dallas snow in 1993. With Miami trailing 14-13 in the closing seconds of the tilt, Dolphins kicker Pete Stoyanovich attempted a 40-yard field goal for the win. The Cowboys blocked the kick — seemingly securing the victory for the home crowd. However, in a blunder for the ages, Cowboys defensive lineman Leon Lett inexplicably attempted to recover the loose football, but slipped on the slick turf, knocking the ball forward. Dolphins center Jeff Dellenbach would jump on the fumble near the Cowboys' goalline, giving Stoyanovich another opportunity to make a field goal from a much shorter distance. He would nail the kick and Miami would win the game by a score of 16-14.

articles.title: How could rain, strong winds affect Bills-Chiefs Thanksgiving game?

Rain and strong winds could make for challenging conditions when the Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

A powerful Thanksgiving storm moving through Western New York is expected to bring heavy rain and gusty winds Thursday night, with conditions deteriorating ahead of the 8:20 p.m. kickoff, according to AccuWeather.

The combination could affect passing, kicking and ball handling.

"A gust at the wrong moment can push a field goal wide or send a deep pass off target. With rain, a slick football can make even a routine catch or handoff harder to secure," AccuWeather Senior Meteorologist Tyler Roys said.

How much rain and wind is expected for Bills-Chiefs?

AccuWeather forecasts a 90% chance of rain Thursday around Highmark Stadium, with east-northeast winds around 18 mph and gusts as high as 37 mph. Thursday night, periods of rain and winds around 20 mph are expected.

The latest forecast favors rain rather than significant snow around the stadium, with temperatures expected to remain above freezing.

Fans should continue to monitor the latest National Weather Service forecast and AccuWeather forecast for Buffalo before heading to Orchard Park because conditions can change leading up to kickoff.

How could rain and wind affect the Bills game?

Wind could complicate field-goal attempts and longer passes, while rain could make the football more difficult to handle, according to Roys.

The weather could also provide an early test for Buffalo's new Highmark Stadium, which opened for the 2026 season. Although a canopy covers much of the seating area, the playing field remains exposed to the elements, according to AccuWeather.

How cold will it feel at the Bills game?

Fans should prepare for a chilly and wet Thanksgiving night.

Temperatures are expected to fall into the 30s, but the combination of rain and wind could make it feel considerably colder. AccuWeather forecasts RealFeel temperatures around 20 degrees throughout the game.

"For fans in the stands, getting wet early could make it tough to stay warm throughout the fourth quarter," Roys said.

The Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions enter Thanksgiving Day with identical 8-2 records and plenty at stake in the NFC North. However, Thursday's game at Ford Field will carry considerably more significance than a battle between two longtime division rivals. The Lions announced Tuesday that Martha Firestone Ford, the franchise's former principal owner, died at the age of 101.

Ford's passing comes less than two years after the death of another influential woman in NFL ownership. Chicago Bears owner Virginia Halas McCaskey died in February 2025 at the age of 102, leaving behind a remarkable connection to the earliest days of professional football.

The timing of Thursday's game provides an opportunity to appreciate two women whose influence extended well beyond their respective franchises.

Martha Firestone Ford and Virginia McCaskey shared a special connection

While the Bears and Lions have spent generations competing against one another, their longtime owners enjoyed a much different relationship. According to the Chicago Sun-Times , Bears chairman George McCaskey described his mother and Ford as close friends in 2020.

Their stories were also featured together in the 2019 NFL Films documentary "A Lifetime of Sundays." The production examined the experiences of four influential women in professional football, including Patricia Rooney of the Pittsburgh Steelers and Norma Hunt of the Kansas City Chiefs .

Interestingly, all four of those franchises are participating in nationally televised games during this year's Thanksgiving football schedule. The Chiefs visit Buffalo on Thursday evening, while Pittsburgh hosts Denver on Black Friday.

Detroit's Thanksgiving tradition carries special significance

Ford assumed principal ownership of the Lions following her husband's death in 2014. Detroit reached the playoffs twice during her six years in charge, and she invested in improvements to Ford Field before transferring leadership responsibilities to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp, in 2020.

The Lions have since developed into one of the NFC's most competitive teams, making Thursday's meeting with Chicago particularly compelling. Both franchises have endured difficult stretches, and their simultaneous emergence as contenders provides another interesting chapter in their longstanding rivalry.

Football fans will understandably spend much of Thanksgiving discussing playoff positioning, quarterback performances and division championship possibilities. For the families connected to these historic organizations, however, Thursday represents something deeper.

Nearly a century of Thanksgiving football has produced countless memorable moments in Detroit. This year's game offers another reminder of the people who helped make that tradition possible.

articles.title: Micah Parsons: Our play in second half Wednesday night was inexcusable
articles.summary: The Rams ran for 195 yards after halftime in their 26-13 win.
articles.body:
Packers defensive end Micah Parsons made his return to the lineup against the Rams on Wednesday night, but he wasn't able to help his team to a win in Los Angeles.

Parsons picked up a sack late in the first half that sent the game to the break with the score tied 13-13, but he couldn't make an impact in the second half because the Rams barely threw the ball. After running 12 times for 46 yards in the first half, the Rams ran 35 times for 194 yards while outscoring the Packers 13-0 in the final 30 minutes.

After the game, Parsons said it is "just inexcusable" to allow opposing teams to "dictate games like that" and said the aftermath has to be an increased level of accountability for the entire defense.

"We need to figure out who's going to be a dog or not," Parsons said. "That's just the reality of it. To me, to be honest and this is around the league, if someone can line up 50 times and run down your mouth and you don't have an answer for it, that is player — that's accountability. That's just how I really feel about it. I wasn't able to get on the field because of it, because they didn't want to waste my plays on first and second down I think the whole thing is just bad and we've got to figure out who's willing to play with us or who's playing against us at this point."

The Packers don't have the luxury of having time to figure things out. The loss dropped them to 6-5 on the season and the makeup of the NFC means that they're going to have to win most of their remaining games to have any chance of advancing to the postseason.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' final NFL pass may have been surprisingly fitting after stunning Steelers release
articles.summary: If Aaron Rodgers has played his final NFL game, the four-time MVP will have accomplished something memorable with his final professional pass.
articles.body:
There probably aren't many people who envisioned Aaron Rodgers spending Thanksgiving as a quarterback without an NFL team. However, that is precisely where the four-time league MVP finds himself after an extraordinary sequence of events involving the Pittsburgh Steelers and head coach Mike McCarthy.

Pittsburgh officially released Rodgers on Wednesday following his appearance on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show." The decision came less than 24 hours after the organization announced that Mason Rudolph would start Friday's game against the Denver Broncos .

Should Rodgers decide that he's played enough professional football, there is at least one interesting detail about how his career potentially concluded.

Aaron Rodgers could finish his career with a touchdown

As NBC Sports' Mike Florio pointed out Wednesday evening, Rodgers' final pass with the Steelers was a touchdown. Whether that becomes the final completion of his professional career remains to be seen, but it would certainly represent a fitting statistical conclusion for one of the most accomplished quarterbacks in league history.

According to Pittsburgh's official announcement, Rodgers has thrown for 68,515 yards and 543 touchdowns across 22 NFL seasons. He has appeared in 274 games, making 267 starts while establishing himself as one of the most productive quarterbacks of his generation.

Sometimes great players don't receive the farewell they deserve. Rodgers' departure from Pittsburgh certainly wasn't accompanied by a traditional retirement ceremony, but his most recent pass at least provided a reminder of what made him special.

Rodgers faces an unexpected Thanksgiving decision

Rodgers had previously indicated that the 2026 season would be his last. Instead of spending the next seven games attempting to guide Pittsburgh into the postseason, he must now determine whether pursuing another opportunity is worthwhile.

The Steelers were 6-4 under Rodgers this season, with the veteran completing 220 passes for 2,241 yards and 16 touchdowns. Those numbers could make him an interesting consideration for a quarterback-needy organization, although interest from another team isn't guaranteed.

Rodgers has already accomplished virtually everything an NFL quarterback could reasonably hope to achieve. Another opportunity might eventually present itself, but there is also something appropriate about leaving the field after completing a touchdown pass.

After everything that has transpired this week, that could become one of the more memorable footnotes in an extraordinary football career.
